findings.description: The distinctness check compares only lexical `resolve()` strings. On supported default macOS filesystems, paths differing only by case can name the same file; symlink or hard-link aliases do too. Such `--report`/`--ledger` values pass this check, and after a successful run `writeFile(paths[2], ...)` overwrites the completed JSONL ledger (or the input plan) while the command reports success; a direct symlink probe showed two lexical paths and replacement of the ledger contents. Canonicalize existing targets and compare filesystem identities, with safe handling for not-yet-created outputs, before opening any path.
findings.failureMode: Case, symlink, or hard-link aliases among CLI paths pass validation and a successful experiment destroys its own replay ledger or plan file.
findings.title: Resolve filesystem aliases before writing

findings.description: The output guard lists only each case/family ID, the family/finding IDs, the primary diff path, and the primary finding file. Training input contains additional source identities that are not listed—for example case-02's finding description includes `factory-host/src/index.ts`, and `input.evidence.repository` includes secondary paths and exact revisions/hashes. If the untrusted proposer copies one of those values into either candidate component, this guard accepts it; correct child decisions can then cause a source-specific pair to be reported as the winner despite the candidate contract requiring case-agnostic text. Build the rejection set from every source identity exposed in the training prompt (with normalized matching), including secondary paths, titles, and revision/blob hashes.
findings.failureMode: A proposer response containing a secondary file path, commit SHA, or evidence identity is accepted and can be promoted as a supposedly general candidate.
findings.title: Block every source identity in proposals

findings.description: Corpus loading assumes every selected base/head object is already present locally. In a shallow checkout, `git diff` exits with `fatal: bad object` before any fixture can load; the exact-head review checkout reproduced this for case-01, so both the new golden test and the experiment entry point fail on that otherwise supported developer configuration. Materialize each required revision before invoking `git diff`/`git show` so the corpus does not depend on preexisting full local history.
findings.failureMode: A shallow developer checkout cannot run the experiment or the now-required golden test because historical commit objects are absent.
findings.title: Handle missing historical Git objects

findings.description: The frozen diff is generated with ambient Git formatting configuration. Settings such as `diff.noprefix=true` or `diff.context=0` change the bytes even with `--no-color --no-ext-diff` (a local probe produced three different hashes), so a supported developer checkout with either global setting fails corpus loading at `Diff mismatch` even though the historical content is exact. Pass explicit prefixes, context, algorithm/heuristic settings (or neutralizing `-c` values) so the hash is independent of user Git configuration.
findings.failureMode: The experiment and golden tests fail on a supported developer host whose global Git diff formatting differs from the defaults used to record the hashes.
findings.title: Freeze Git diff formatting before hashing

findings.description: Completed replay recomputes and byte-compares only `prior.result`, then returns `prior.report` verbatim. If the result row's report is accidentally edited or corrupted—for example its token totals, served model, or outcome is changed while the cached calls and result remain intact—`verifyReplayInventory` still passes and zero-call replay reports the altered measurements as valid. Recompute `report(ledger.rows, manifest, replayed)` and reject the replay unless it exactly matches the stored report.
findings.failureMode: A completed ledger with a corrupted stored report replays successfully and returns false measurements.
findings.title: Verify the stored report during replay

findings.description: The fixture declares `context.input.baseSha` as its runtime provenance source and copies that value into every `executingRuntimeSha`. In the production ingest path, however, `baseSha` is assigned from GitHub's `merge_base_commit.sha`; it identifies the reviewed repository base, not the revision of the deployed process executing the workflow. Consequently the new continuity outputs assert a shared runtime and post-deploy provenance that the source data does not establish, invalidating the main runtime-provenance result. Record an actual deployment/build SHA from the runtime snapshot, or mark runtime provenance unavailable rather than relabeling the merge base.
findings.failureMode: When the deployed panel runtime differs from a PR's merge base (for example deployment lags or the branch was based on an older default-branch commit), the report emits the merge-base SHA as `executingRuntimeSha` and falsely attributes the review result to that runtime.
findings.title: Do not label the PR merge base as the executing runtime

findings.description: `eval:continuity` accepts an alternate fixture path, but continuity state is accumulated in raw JSON array order even though each run carries the canonical `round` field. Reordering the same records passes `assertFixture` and changes which families are reported as new versus cross-round repeats (the aggregate changes from 70.4 to 73.5), so deterministic per-round output depends on serialization order. Validate a unique ascending round sequence or sort a validated copy by `round` before accumulation.
findings.failureMode: For a schema-valid fixture whose `panelRuns` array lists round 2 before round 1, round 2's families are treated as first-seen and round 1 is reported as repeating them, yielding incorrect per-round continuity output.
findings.title: Order runs by their round number before computing continuity

findings.description: The fixture declares `runtimeProvenanceField: "context.input.baseSha"` and copies that value into every `executingRuntimeSha`, but GitHub ingestion derives `baseSha` from `comparison.data.merge_base_commit.sha`; it identifies the reviewed diff's merge base, not the deployed factory-host build. When the service executes commit X while reviewing a PR whose merge base is Y, `eval:continuity` and the default metrics output falsely report Y as the executing runtime. Capture an actual build/deployment revision in the stored run and use that field, or leave runtime provenance explicitly unvalidated.
findings.failureMode: A panel run performed by a deployment newer than the PR merge base is published as having executed the merge-base commit, invalidating the runtime-provenance continuity result.
findings.title: Do not treat the PR merge base as the executing runtime SHA

findings.description: The chronology check only requires each round number to increase, so `[1, 3]` is accepted even though round 2 is absent. For a fixture whose contract is to reconstruct the complete panel sequence, this makes a missing run indistinguishable from a valid history and computes repeat/yield metrics across the gap. Require each `run.round` to equal the previous round plus one (starting at 1), and ideally cross-check timestamp order as well.
findings.failureMode: A selected continuity fixture missing an intermediate panel run passes validation and publishes incomplete cross-round metrics as a complete sequence.
findings.title: Reject gaps in the frozen round sequence

findings.description: The authority guard accepts either enum value independently of `githubReviewId`. Thus an unpublished run with `githubReviewId: null` can be labeled `authoritative` (or a published review labeled pending), and the evaluator will silently report the wrong authoritative/pending totals—the exact distinction this slice is intended to preserve. Require authoritative runs to carry a valid review ID and pending-replay runs not to carry one.
findings.failureMode: A selected fixture marks an unpublished panel success authoritative, causing the report to overstate authoritative continuity and hide the pending replay.
findings.title: Bind authority to publication evidence

findings.description: The guard validates `snapshotRunId` and `reviewedHeadSha` independently but never checks the run ID's `panel:<headSha>:` component against the declared reviewed head. A typo or copied snapshot ID can therefore associate one run's appearances with another head and still be emitted as valid per-round provenance. Reject a run unless its snapshot ID encodes the same reviewed head SHA.
findings.failureMode: A panel snapshot copied under the wrong reviewed head passes validation, causing per-round continuity metrics to attribute its findings to the wrong code revision.
findings.title: Bind each snapshot identity to its reviewed head

findings.description: `assertFixture` iterates appearances without validating the `appearance.adjudication` ordinal. A selected schema-v1 fixture can therefore duplicate one appearance, omit another, and reuse the same adjudication number while still exiting successfully; the evaluator then reports inflated appearance, repeat, duplicate, and calibration totals for a sequence it calls complete. Validate that each run's adjudication identities are positive, unique, and cover the run's appearance sequence before computing metrics.
findings.failureMode: A truncated or accidentally duplicated run fixture passes validation and produces a successful but incorrect continuity report instead of rejecting incomplete adjudication evidence.
findings.title: Reject duplicate or missing adjudication identities

findings.description: An appearance is admitted after checking only family, fingerprint, disposition, and blocking; its `judgeState` and `evidence` anchor are never validated. Removing those fields from an otherwise valid selected fixture still yields a successful report and counts the row toward the AC-5 continuity metrics even though it can no longer be traced to an adjudication or changed line. Validate the judge state and a non-empty title/file with a positive evidence line before counting the appearance.
findings.failureMode: A truncated adjudication with no source anchor passes validation and is published as part of the complete continuity sequence.
findings.title: Require source evidence on every counted appearance

findings.description: The Open SWE validator checks only a local string ID and family, while the report counts every entry as a genuine thread without validating `reviewId` or `reviewedHeadSha`. A selected fixture containing a fabricated or truncated thread such as `{id:'x', family:'evidence-manifest-exposure'}` passes and inflates `threads`; require a positive source review ID and a valid reviewed-head SHA before admitting it to the comparison.
findings.failureMode: An Open SWE record with no source review or head provenance is accepted as a genuine thread and changes the published comparison metrics.
findings.title: Validate Open SWE source provenance before counting a thread

findings.description: The consistency guard rejects only `accepted` appearances for a family marked `real: false`; a `deferred` appearance for the same non-real family passes and is added to `deferredFamilies`. That produces an impossible report where a family classified as not real is nevertheless counted as a real unresolved defect (and can even yield `deferredFamilies: 1` with `realFamilies: 0`). Apply the real-family requirement to both accepted and deferred dispositions.
findings.failureMode: A contradictory non-real/deferred fixture is accepted and publishes internally inconsistent family-yield metrics instead of being rejected.
findings.title: Reject deferred dispositions on non-real families

findings.description: Registering tag `287` here makes it loadable, but the scoring path calls `loadFrozenDiff` for any anchored finding and requires exactly one file under `phase-a/dataset/diffs`. This fixture adds no dataset diff, so scoring a normal account finding exits with ENOENT before producing metrics. Add the frozen diff at the scorer's required path (and include/validate it as part of the fixture).
findings.failureMode: Run `evals/golden/match.mjs` against this fixture with a finding anchored to one of its labels; the scorer exits while scanning the missing `phase-a/dataset/diffs` directory instead of generating a score.
findings.title: Registered fixture cannot run through the scorer

findings.description: Captured lane fixtures use the production `Patches:\n### <path>` aggregate format, and `auditVisibility` recognizes files only from those `###` markers. This fixture instead puts a raw `diff --git` stream in `input.diff`; once the missing frozen diff is supplied, the auditor classifies all three labels as absent from the ingest diff and functional-only scoring excludes the entire positive cohort. Build `input.diff` from the per-file patches in the production aggregate format.
findings.failureMode: Audit tag 287 for scoring after supplying its separate frozen diff; all three anchored labels are reported `notVisible` with `anchor lines absent from ingest diff`, leaving zero scorable positives.
findings.title: Ingest diff uses the wrong format for visibility auditing

findings.description: This object records 11 deletions and `@@ -1,13 +1,5 @@`, but the hunk contains only 9 deleted lines and 11 old-side lines. A standard patch parser therefore rejects the aggregate fixture (`git apply --numstat` reports a corrupt patch), so the supposedly executable frozen input cannot be reconstructed. Record 9 deletions, use the actual `-1,11` extent, and update the duplicate hunk in `input.diff`.
findings.failureMode: Load this golden fixture and try to parse/apply `input.diff`; parsing stops at the job-replacement hunk instead of reconstructing the six-case cohort.
findings.title: Job-replacement fixture contains a corrupt unified-diff hunk

findings.description: The recorded patch claims 8 deletions and a 10-line old hunk, while its body has 7 deletions and 9 old-side lines. Once the preceding corrupt hunk is fixed, patch parsing will fail here as well, preventing reconstruction of this paired control. Change the deletion count to 7 and the header to `@@ -1,9 +1,5 @@` in both representations.
findings.failureMode: Parse/apply the corrected aggregate fixture through the job-selection section; its inconsistent header leaves the golden input corrupt and unusable as an executable diff.
findings.title: Job-selection fixture has incorrect hunk and deletion counts

findings.description: The object records 14 additions/5 deletions and `@@ -1,7 +1,16 @@`, but the hunk actually has 12 additions, 2 deletions, 5 old lines, and 15 new lines. After earlier hunks are repaired, this malformed hunk still makes the executable fixture unparseable. Use the actual metadata/header and make the aggregate `input.diff` match.
findings.failureMode: Parse/apply the fixture through provider-rows; the false old/new extents make the patch corrupt rather than yielding the labeled provider behavior.
findings.title: Provider-rows fixture substantially overstates both sides of its patch

findings.description: This control records 16 additions/5 deletions and `@@ -1,7 +1,18 @@`, although its body has 14 additions, 2 deletions, 5 old lines, and 17 new lines. Fixing the other three malformed hunks would still leave reconstruction failing at this final section. Use the actual counts/header in the per-file patch and aggregate diff.
findings.failureMode: Parse/apply the otherwise-corrected fixture through provider-summary; the final malformed hunk is rejected, so the paired negative control cannot be reconstructed.
findings.title: Provider-summary control also has invalid patch metadata

findings.description: The tests execute newly hand-written `read`, `before`/`after`, and provider functions rather than reconstructing the code in the fixture. This is already masking the four malformed fixture hunks: `test:golden` passes even though their recorded headers/stats disagree with their bodies and a patch parser rejects the aggregate diff. Reconstruct and execute the before/after modules from each recorded patch, compare after-source with `repositoryContent`, and bind labels to those lines so invalid experiment input fails CI.
findings.failureMode: Run `test:golden` on the committed malformed fixture; all behavior-preservation tests pass, falsely certifying an input that cannot be reconstructed as a unified diff.
findings.title: Behavior tests validate replicas instead of the frozen fixture

findings.description: The changed report says the baseline was 27/27, the candidate fell to 26/27, and later says five conditions failed. The PR's stated corrected reset is baseline 25/27 versus candidate 27/27 with only the cross-provider gain condition failing. Merging this file therefore publishes the superseded experiment metrics and wrong gate application as the durable result; update the report to the corrected 36-record reset.
findings.failureMode: A reader or later optimizer uses this committed experiment record and concludes the candidate reduced recall/precision for five reasons, although the registered reset says it improved both and failed only the provider-family condition.
findings.title: Report records the invalidated run instead of the reset results

findings.description: On the default native OpenAI judge path, the provider's `response.created` model is exposed by AI SDK as `response.modelId`; because it equals the configured bare model, this condition discards it and the successful generation plus `judgeModelReported` are emitted as null. This loses provider identity on the evaluator's mainline route. Capture that provider event (or otherwise trust this provider-specific response metadata) rather than suppressing an exact match.
findings.failureMode: A normal native OpenAI adjudication succeeds with a provider-reported model matching the request, but provenance records `modelReported: null` and downstream ensemble output loses the actual judge identity.
findings.title: Preserve matching provider-reported model IDs

findings.description: Panel `mustFix` entries are findings directly, but actual `waived` entries have the shape `{ finding, reason, basis }`. Searching every row via `row.fingerprint` and then checking `matched.severity` means a valid calibrated waived finding can never match; converting the existing PR 194 item to the repository's real waived shape causes `Panel finding drift`. Normalize waived rows to `row.finding` before fingerprint/severity matching, while retaining `blocking: false`.
findings.failureMode: Any otherwise valid development-calibration session containing a waived panel finding is rejected by validation.
findings.title: Read waived finding fields from the nested finding

findings.description: `RegExp.test` coerces non-strings, so the Git-SHA checks accept one-element arrays containing valid SHAs; the same applies to panel projection/pack hashes and session policy hashes. This leaves array-valued provenance in a validated corpus and can make head grouping/equality incorrect. Require `typeof value === 'string'` before every `GIT_SHA`/`SHA` regex, retaining explicit `null` only where allowed.
findings.failureMode: Malformed array-valued commit or hash provenance passes validation and produces wrong provenance/phase-comparison shapes.
findings.title: Require string types before hash regex checks

findings.description: This only checks each declared finding against a panel row; it never checks that every `mustFix`/`waived` row was declared, nor that two findings do not reuse the same fingerprint. Removing a finding from a calibrated panel session still validates and changes the reported-family count, while duplicating one also validates. Compare the complete fingerprint sets/cardinalities for each calibrated panel session.
findings.failureMode: A calibrated corpus with an omitted or multiply mapped panel finding passes validation and produces incorrect family-level metrics.
findings.title: Enforce an exhaustive one-to-one panel mapping

findings.description: The final history check only verifies that each `priorSessionIds` value exists somewhere in the record. A corpus where session A names B as prior and B names A (or a session names itself) passes validation, so malformed cyclic chronology is accepted even though this validator is intended to enforce acyclic declared session history. Traverse the prior-session graph and reject self-references and cycles.
findings.failureMode: Calling validateAdjudicationCorpus with mutually dependent or self-dependent sessions returns successfully instead of rejecting invalid session chronology.
findings.title: Reject cyclic declared session history

findings.description: The inventory comparison binds only derived artifact IDs to raw GitHub IDs. `validateArtifact` hashes an artifact against its own stored hash, but nothing compares a review/comment artifact's `content` and `commitSha` with the matching raw object's `body` and `commit_id`. Consequently forged review evidence with a recomputed hash is accepted while the untouched authoritative raw source says something else. Build the raw-object map and validate each extracted GitHub artifact's bytes and provenance against it.
findings.failureMode: A corpus whose extracted review evidence or commit binding disagrees with its frozen authoritative GitHub bytes passes validation and can drive false calibration labels and metrics.
findings.title: Bind artifact bytes to their raw source records

findings.description: A session head is only syntax-checked. It is never compared with the commit SHA of the source review/panel artifact, or with `evidence.headSha`/PR number when the full panel record contains them. Thus assigning both systems the same unrelated head still yields `phase-matched`, and a panel record whose embedded provenance names PR 999 also validates. Require the session, artifact, and available full-record provenance to agree before phase matching.
findings.failureMode: Forged or miscopied reviewed-head/panel provenance passes validation and can report a false phase-matched comparison.
findings.title: Verify reviewed heads against authoritative session evidence

findings.description: `crossRoundRepetitions` treats every earlier array entry for the same PR/system as prior history, ignoring both `session.priorSessionIds` and the finding's declared history state. Two disconnected sessions that each label a family as new therefore still count as a cross-round repetition. Follow the validated prior-session graph (and enforce consistency with history states) rather than relying on record insertion order.
findings.failureMode: Independent review histories sharing a family ID are reported as cross-round repetition, so the declared-history repetition metric is wrong.
findings.title: Compute repetitions from declared session history

findings.description: `severityDispositionErrors` only compares the finding's blocking flag with the family's delivery disposition; it never compares `finding.reportedSeverity` with the adjudicated `family.consequenceSeverity`. Changing a proven family's consequence from medium to low leaves the metric at 2, so a pure severity error is silently omitted despite the stored consequence-severity axis and the advertised severity/disposition report. Count a family when either classification disagrees.
findings.failureMode: A review that gets blocking disposition right but assigns the wrong consequence severity is reported as having no severity/disposition error.
findings.title: Include severity mismatches in the error metric

findings.description: Reviewer and judge pack hashes are syntax-checked, but `packs.rereads` is only checked to be an array; each reread's `pack.hash` is ignored. Replacing a real reread hash with `not-a-hash` still passes, so the validator accepts malformed provenance for the additional context actually served to a reviewer. Iterate rereads and require each nested pack hash to be a string SHA-256.
findings.failureMode: A corpus with corrupt or missing reread-pack provenance passes hash validation.
findings.title: Validate every reread pack hash

findings.description: The panel-record completeness check validates `served`, `reviews`, and `adjudications` but omits `result.mustFix` and `result.waived`, even though `validateSession` later spreads those fields. A panel record with both verdict lists deleted passes whenever its (for example excluded) session has no finding rows, leaving a purported full panel record incomplete; if a finding is later added, validation crashes with a raw iterable TypeError instead. Include both verdict lists in the artifact shape check.
findings.failureMode: An incomplete full panel record is accepted for sessions without findings, or produces an uncontrolled TypeError when findings are present.
findings.title: Validate the panel verdict lists as required arrays

findings.description: The record source fields are only SHA-shaped; the validator never compares `record.pullRequest`/`record.source` with the frozen pull response's `number`, base/head SHAs, and merge SHA. A raw response for another PR or commit set can therefore be self-hashed and accepted under this manifest slot, undermining the claimed exact PR interval. Parse the required pull source and cross-check its identity and SHAs.
findings.failureMode: A record containing a mismatched raw pull response passes validation and is reported as calibration evidence for the wrong PR/head.
findings.title: Bind each record to its raw pull source

findings.description: The Open SWE branch validates only findings that the corpus already declares. It neither requires every finding-bearing review comment in the session to have a finding row nor prevents multiple rows from reusing one comment. Removing the calibrated PR 196 finding, or duplicating it under a new ID, still validates; the omission lowers the reported blocking-family count. Parse the review-comment markers and compare them one-to-one with `session.findings`.
findings.failureMode: An omitted or duplicate Open SWE finding mapping passes validation and yields incorrect precision and family counts.
findings.title: Enforce exhaustive Open SWE finding extraction

findings.description: A family's disposition source is checked only for existence, not for the `disposition-evidence` calibration status used by every real disposition in the fixture. Pointing the proven PR 196 family at its ordinary review container still validates, so a family can be labeled must-fix/dismissed without any operator disposition evidence and will affect precision. Require the referenced artifact to be disposition evidence (and an appropriate review-comment/operator-disposition kind).
findings.failureMode: An unsupported human disposition passes corpus validation and is counted as calibration ground truth.
findings.title: Require disposition evidence for calibrated families

findings.description: The finding source must belong to the session, but its calibration status is never checked. A development session/family can therefore cite a source explicitly marked `excluded`; validation still succeeds and `developmentRows` counts it in precision. Require each scored finding source to be `development-calibration` (while allowing separate disposition-evidence artifacts only for adjudication).
findings.failureMode: Evidence explicitly excluded from calibration is accepted as a development finding and contaminates reported precision.
findings.title: Exclude findings backed by excluded artifacts

findings.description: The condition records `response.modelId` only when its bare value differs from the configured model. On the default native OpenAI stream, Mastra's `response.modelId` is populated from the provider's `response.created.response.model`; when the provider normally reports the requested `gpt-5.6-sol` exactly, this condition suppresses that real evidence and emits `modelReported: null`, so successful ensemble records lose the judge identity this change is meant to preserve. Distinguish the Claude wrapper's configured fallback from native AI-SDK responses (for example with lane/provider provenance) and trust the native response field even when it matches the request.
findings.failureMode: A normal default native OpenAI judge response reports `gpt-5.6-sol`, equal to the request; the resulting successful generation records `modelReported: null` rather than the provider-reported identity.
findings.title: Native responses lose matching provider model identity

findings.description: Native decisions at line 737 and the Claude decision calls at lines 759, 765, and 771 assign `result` only after the SDK has already validated structured output. When a provider returns a completed, billable response whose JSON violates the decision schema, that validation throws before assignment; the catch emits null model/usage, and a successful repair leaves the aggregate incomplete and undercounts usage. The OpenAI stream still exposes its response and usage after the failure, and the SDKs support a nonthrowing validation strategy, so retain/capture completion metadata and perform the throwing schema parse only after the full result is available.
findings.failureMode: Any native or Claude decision response that reaches the provider but fails structured-output validation is repaired, yet the first completed call is recorded with modelReported/usage null and omitted from known aggregate usage.
findings.title: Structured-output repairs lose completed-call metadata

findings.description: The native OpenAI streaming provider populates `response.modelId` from the provider's `response.created.model`, but this condition drops it whenever it equals the requested bare model. On the default `openai/gpt-5.6-sol` judge path, a normal event reporting `gpt-5.6-sol` therefore produces `modelReported: null`; only an unexpected/suffixed model is retained. An executed provider fixture reproduced `gpt-5.6-sol => null` while `gpt-5.6-sol-live` was retained. Distinguish the Claude SDK's configured fallback from the native OpenAI provider response instead of treating equality as absence of evidence.
findings.failureMode: A successful default native OpenAI judge response reports the exact requested model, yet the ensemble records `judgeModelReported` as null.
findings.title: Keep the native OpenAI response model

findings.description: `runSummary` previously defaulted a returned record with no `usage` to zero/null counters, but this changed line unconditionally dereferences `record.usage`. An injected `options.ensemble` that returns a failed or legacy record without usage now makes `runBaseline` throw `TypeError` while building the manifest instead of recording that run; retain optional/defaulted counters and mark completeness false.
findings.failureMode: Calling exported runBaseline with an injected ensemble that returns a record lacking usage crashes during records.map(runSummary).
findings.title: Keep baseline summaries tolerant of missing usage

findings.description: The total maps an absent `item.usage` (or a usage object with no `total`) to zero, but the new completeness check tests only `item.usage !== null`; `undefined` and `{}` are therefore accepted as known. Such a lane makes `runEnsemble` report `usage.complete: true` even though its token total is unavailable. Base completeness on `usageTotal(item.usage) !== null` rather than object nullness.
findings.failureMode: A successful lane record without a usable usage total plus a judge with known usage produces an ensemble whose usage.complete is incorrectly true.
findings.title: Treat absent lane totals as incomplete

findings.description: On the default native OpenAI judge path, Mastra returns the provider's `response.created.response.model` as `result.response.modelId`, while this extractor only inspects `response.body.model` and Claude metadata. A normal successful `openai/gpt-5.6-sol` adjudication therefore records `generation.modelReported: null` and `runEnsemble` emits `judgeModelReported: null` even though the provider reported its model. Extract the native AI-SDK response identity with provider-aware handling so Claude's configured identity is not mistaken for evidence.
findings.failureMode: A successful default native OpenAI adjudication produces a false unknown model identity in generation provenance and ensemble output.
findings.title: Native OpenAI's reported model is discarded

findings.description: For a native Anthropic decision, Mastra's top-level usage reports `inputTokens` including both `cachedInputTokens` and `cacheCreationInputTokens`. This fallback subtracts only cached reads, so a response with 7 uncached, 3 cache-read, 2 cache-write and 5 output is recorded as `{input:9,cached:3,cacheCreation:2,output:5,total:17}`: the components add to 19 and the uncached-input field is overstated by 2. Subtract cache creation as well for this normalized top-level shape while retaining raw Anthropic snake-case semantics.
findings.failureMode: Any native Anthropic decision that creates prompt-cache entries emits internally inconsistent provenance and overstates aggregate `input` usage.
findings.title: Cached Anthropic writes are counted as uncached input

findings.description: The new decision provenance trusts any finite provider total, including negative or fractional values. The pinned native xAI path accepts a response such as `prompt_tokens:-10, completion_tokens:5, total_tokens:-5`, and this code emits a successful generation with `usage.total:-5`; aggregation then subtracts tokens from the ensemble's measured cost. Reject non-integer/negative usage fields (record the attempt's usage as unknown) rather than treating malformed vendor metadata as valid.
findings.failureMode: A malformed provider usage object reaches a supported native decision call and corrupts aggregate/baseline usage with a negative token total.
findings.title: Malformed usage can produce negative totals

findings.description: The default native OpenAI decision path exposes the provider's `response.created.response.model` as `result.response.modelId`, while its full output has no `response.body.model` and `providerMetadata.openai` contains only `responseId`. This function ignores `response.modelId`, so a successful default `openai/gpt-5.6-sol` adjudication records `modelReported: null` and `runEnsemble` also emits a null judge identity even though the provider reported it. Keep ignoring that field for the Claude SDK wrapper, where it is configured, but allow the native harness to pass/trust its provider-reported `response.modelId`.
findings.failureMode: Every successful default native OpenAI judge call drops an available provider-reported model identity and emits null provenance.
findings.title: Retain native OpenAI's reported model identity

findings.description: When Mastra returns its normal numeric `LanguageModelUsage` shape for an Anthropic decision (for example uncached 7, cache-read 3, cache-created 2, output 5), this fallback delegates to `normalizeUsage`, which subtracts only cached reads from the 12 total input tokens and records `input: 9` instead of 7. Native Anthropic's cache middleware can produce cache writes on a normal first call, so the recorded fields sum to 19 while `total` is 17 and evaluator usage is overstated. Normalize this shape from its `usage.raw` V3 input/output breakdown.
findings.failureMode: A native Anthropic decision with nonzero prompt-cache creation reports inflated uncached input/token accounting and internally inconsistent provenance.
findings.title: Subtract cache-write tokens from decision input usage

findings.description: This changes `judgePromptHash` from the same static instruction hash on every run to the exact provider prompt hash, which varies with each tag's findings, context, and diff. `runBaseline` still stores only `records.find(...).judgePromptHash` at the manifest top level and `runSummary` omits the per-run hash, so a multi-tag baseline silently labels the whole baseline with the first judged tag's hash and loses the other calls' hashes from the manifest. Put `record.judgePromptHash` into every run summary and remove the now-invalid baseline-wide singular value.
findings.failureMode: A normal baseline over multiple tags emits a manifest with one tag's exact judge prompt hash presented as the provenance for all runs, while all other hashes are absent.
findings.title: Preserve each baseline run's dynamic judge hash

findings.description: `child_process.spawn()` returns a `ChildProcess` even when the executable is missing and then emits `error`; calling `onInvoked` immediately therefore turns an `ENOENT`/`EACCES` launch failure into a failed model generation with unknown usage. Evaluator provenance then claims a provider attempt happened and marks usage incomplete although no Codex process or provider call ran. Set the marker from the child's `spawn` event (which is not emitted on launch failure) rather than immediately after construction.
findings.failureMode: A missing or non-executable Codex binary creates a false GenerationAttempt and falsely incomplete usage even though no model call occurred.
findings.title: Mark Codex invoked only after a successful spawn

findings.description: The new `factory-automation` audience makes an org-scoped credential win, and Factory 0.10 defines org-scoped rows as shared API keys. Every native dispatch still constructs an OAuth-only wrapper, though: Anthropic rejects `api_key` explicitly, while xAI and OpenAI report “Not logged in.” Thus a valid org API key shadowing the fallback user's OAuth makes real golden lanes fail instead of run. The same new audience is used in `ensemble.mjs:59`, `match.mjs:111`, and `optimize/pilot.mjs:38`; add API-key-capable native routing for the selected credential so all four automation entry points can honor org-first precedence.
findings.failureMode: With both an org-scoped API key and a user-scoped OAuth row for a provider, any real golden lane/judge selects and caches the org key, then its OAuth-only request wrapper aborts before the provider request.
findings.title: Route org API keys through an API-key-capable native provider

findings.description: This explicitly disables both the transaction's 20-second `statement_timeout` and any role/database default before the UPDATE and COMMIT. If that write executes a slow trigger or stalls on database work that is not lock acquisition, `lock_timeout` does not apply and `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout` does not fire during the active query, so `getApiKey()` can hold its pool client indefinitely. Keep a finite write-phase statement timeout; the new `lockTimedOut` flag already prevents post-lock `57014` failures from entering lock-wait recovery.
findings.failureMode: With a slow/stalled UPDATE (for example a long-running trigger), credential access hangs indefinitely and repeated calls can exhaust the pool instead of failing after the configured statement timeout.
findings.title: Keep a timeout on post-lock writes

findings.description: The distinctness check compares only `resolve()`d path strings, not filesystem identity. If `--report report-link` is a symlink to the plan or ledger, all three strings pass the check; after the experiment, `writeFile(paths[2], ...)` follows the alias and truncates the plan or complete ledger. Resolve existing symlink targets and/or open outputs with no-follow/exclusive semantics before execution.
findings.failureMode: An operator supplies lexically distinct plan, ledger, and report names where the report is a symlink/hardlink to another artifact; successful completion destroys that artifact when writing the report.
findings.title: Symlinked output paths bypass alias protection and overwrite run artifacts

findings.description: `loadAdjudicationExperimentCases()` now unconditionally runs `git diff`/`git show` against old reviewed-head SHAs. On a supported macOS developer checkout whose Git repository is shallow and lacks those objects, `pnpm test:golden` fails at module initialization with `fatal: bad object ...` rather than running the suite. The new package script always includes this test, while only GitHub CI explicitly fetches full history. Store the frozen diff/blob bytes as fixtures or otherwise make the loader handle/fetch missing historical objects before invoking Git.
findings.failureMode: A supported developer runs the golden tests from a shallow clone; loading the new corpus throws on the first absent historical SHA and aborts the test suite.
findings.title: Historical Git objects make the golden suite crash in shallow clones

findings.description: The replay path recomputes and compares only `prior.result`, then returns `prior.report` verbatim. If the completed ledger's result row has a valid-JSON report changed by corruption or editing while its call/cache rows and result remain intact, `verifyReplayInventory` passes and zero-call replay emits the altered metrics/usage report as valid. Recompute `report(ledger.rows, manifest, replayed)` during replay and compare it with the stored report before returning it.
findings.failureMode: A completed ledger has only its stored report modified; replay succeeds and publishes wrong experiment metrics instead of reporting replay divergence.
findings.title: Replay trusts the stored report instead of recomputing it

findings.description: `verifyReplayInventory` correlates operation IDs and replay keys but never recomputes `requestHash` from the intent's `request`, compares intent/terminal request hashes, or checks the recorded input/system/schema/model fields against the frozen operation. Changing a completed intent's prompt or route metadata therefore leaves replay green and presents fabricated call evidence even though live execution would reject that drift. Recompute each intent hash and validate all frozen request/route fields (and matching terminal hashes) before accepting a completed replay.
findings.failureMode: A completed ledger's model-call intent is corrupted or edited while cache/result rows stay intact; zero-call replay succeeds with false provenance for what prompt/model was served.
findings.title: Replay never authenticates the recorded request evidence

findings.description: `roundFingerprints` is recreated for each run, so `exactFingerprintDuplicates` only detects duplicates inside one round. The frozen fixture repeats fingerprint `v1:7cfad...` in rounds 8 and 9, yet this evaluator reports 0; maintain a suite-wide seen-fingerprint set (or a separate prior-round set) so the advertised exact cross-round duplicate is reported.
findings.failureMode: Running `pnpm eval:continuity` on the bundled PR 195 fixture emits `panel.exactFingerprintDuplicates: 0` even though the same exact fingerprint appears in rounds 8 and 9, producing a wrong primary evaluation metric.
findings.title: Count exact fingerprints across rounds

findings.description: The panel finding “Canonical panel runs omit their evidence manifest” is assigned `evidence-manifest-exposure`, while the Open SWE thread from the same reviewed head and resolved by the same `e93c...` commit is assigned `inner-run-manifest`. These are the shared concrete defect this slice is meant to canonicalize, but the differing keys make every family-key join report zero Panel/Open SWE overlap. Assign both records one canonical family ID.
findings.failureMode: Any comparison or aggregate deduplicating Panel and Open SWE records by the fixture's family key overcounts unique defect families and reports no shared defect for PR 195.
findings.title: Canonicalize the shared manifest family

findings.description: This registers continuity only as a separate command; `eval:metrics` still executes the unchanged `metrics.mjs`, which neither imports nor computes the new continuity metrics. Therefore the advertised default metrics output omits the PR-195 yield, duplicate, and calibration data. Compose continuity into `eval:metrics` (and its JSON output) rather than exposing it solely through `eval:continuity`.
findings.failureMode: A consumer or CI job running the documented default `pnpm eval:metrics` path receives only the existing six arm records, with no continuity metrics at all.
findings.title: Include continuity in the default metrics command

findings.description: The account/preference pair is distinguishable only if the reviewer can see that `Client.read` defaults `cache` to true, but the model-facing context on this line does not say so. `src/client.js` is placed in `repositoryContent`, yet assembling the exact production context/pack hashes reported by this PR confirms that both the class and its default are omitted while both argument removals are shown. A reviewer therefore cannot know which removal is the positive and can be scored wrong for refusing to guess (or can emit the documented preference-control false positive). Include the default in `input.context` or otherwise make `src/client.js` rendered evidence, then rerun because this changes model input.
findings.failureMode: Run a baseline or candidate lane on tag 287. The reviewer sees cache:false and cache:true both replaced by the same argument-less call, plus the source-of-truth requirement, but no Client implementation/default. It cannot determine whether account or preferences changed behavior, so account misses and preference findings measure hidden evidence rather than behavior-preservation capability and can change the reported gate metrics.
findings.title: Expose the cache default in the reviewer context

findings.description: Tag 287 is registered as a train fixture, but the new tree contains no `phase-a/dataset/diffs` entry. With any anchored finding, the supported `match.mjs --fixtures evals/golden/fixtures/mastra-287` path therefore exits with ENOENT before scoring. Although programmatic callers can work around this by passing `opts.diff`, the CLI has no such option; add `phase-a/dataset/diffs/287_behavior-preservation.diff` (matching `input.diff`) so the retained fixture can actually reproduce the reported scorer runs.
findings.failureMode: Run the match scorer against tag 287 with a lane record containing the labeled account finding. Tier-1 produces a candidate, `loadFrozenDiff` scans the absent phase-a/dataset/diffs directory, and the CLI exits 1 without a score file.
findings.title: Ship the raw diff required by the scorer

findings.description: The default policy here, and the matching default in `evals/golden/ensemble.mjs`, now make the native OpenAI adjudicator the mainline judge, but that path parses only `result.object` and never checks the response's reported model identity. If the OAuth endpoint serves an alias or different model with schema-valid decisions, both service and eval accept the verdict as GPT-5.6 Sol; the sibling native `generateText` path rejects this mismatch. Add the same identity check to `runNativeAdjudicator` (including stream results).
findings.failureMode: A schema-valid response served by a model other than gpt-5.6-sol is accepted as the default Sol adjudication and can produce the wrong merge verdict and evaluation record.
findings.title: Verify the model served by the new default native judge

findings.description: Defaulting `productionJudge` to `native` makes both fidelity and scope-replay CLI calls enter the credential branch on every unconfigured run. That branch imports its credential dependencies only from `~/.local/share/mastra`, so a supported macOS developer checkout with valid credential env but no separate deployed tree now fails with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`; before this line changed, the default Claude path used the checkout's static harness import and never touched that tree. Resolve these modules from the checkout (or fall back to it) when selecting the new default native judge.
findings.failureMode: The fidelity and scope-replay eval entry points fail before adjudication on a developer host that has the repository build and credentials but no ~/.local/share/mastra deployment.
findings.title: Keep default eval adjudication runnable from a checkout

findings.description: This resolver differs from server startup in two supported configurations: a native fallback with no `PANEL_JUDGE_NATIVE_MODEL` receives no model, while an explicitly blank model is silently replaced with Sol. Consequently a Claude-primary/native-fallback eval fails on a Claude outage even though the service would recover, and a blank-model eval runs although the service rejects that configuration. Base the default on `(primary === 'native' || fallback === 'native')` and only apply it when the variable is undefined.
findings.failureMode: Golden ensemble/fidelity routes native judge attempts differently from the identically configured service, causing failed or misleading evaluation runs.
findings.title: Match native-model defaults in the evaluator

findings.description: The raw-source check hashes each source and inventories only review IDs; it never compares each extracted review/review-comment/operator artifact's body or commit SHA with the matching raw GitHub object (nor the record source fields with the raw pull). Thus a self-hashed fabricated review comment with an existing ID is accepted and can still support scored findings—the PR 196 source comment can be replaced by arbitrary `🟡` text while Open SWE precision remains reported as 100%. Build the artifact map from the parsed raw objects and require the extracted content/provenance to match before scoring.
findings.failureMode: A self-consistent but incorrectly extracted or edited corpus validates and reports calibration from evidence that is absent from the authoritative frozen response.
findings.title: Bind artifacts to the hashed GitHub sources

findings.description: Each panel finding is only checked with `find`, so the validator never proves a one-to-one, exhaustive match against `result.mustFix`/`result.waived`. A corpus can omit a real panel finding or repeat one fingerprint under a new finding ID and still validate; metrics then silently change (for example, omitting PR 200's hunk finding changes precision from 60% to 50%, while duplicating a fingerprint creates a false within-round duplicate). Compare the two inventories as unique fingerprint multisets and reject omissions, duplicates, and extra mappings for calibrated panel sessions.
findings.failureMode: A malformed calibrated panel session is accepted and produces incorrect precision or repetition metrics.
findings.title: Require an exact panel finding inventory

findings.description: The Open SWE branch validates only findings that happen to be listed; it never requires every development-calibration finding comment in the session to appear once. Removing PR 196's sole finding still passes validation and silently reduces Open SWE's accepted/reported inventory from 2 to 1, while duplicating a source comment under a new finding ID is likewise allowed. Compare session findings one-to-one with the calibrated Open SWE finding artifacts instead of checking only each provided row.
findings.failureMode: An omitted or duplicated Open SWE finding is accepted and the reported system calibration inventory is wrong.
findings.title: Require an exact Open SWE finding inventory

findings.description: `repetitionMetrics` treats every earlier array entry for the same PR/system as history and never reads `session.priorSessionIds`. For independent branches (or merely a different serialization order), it reports cross-round repetitions that are not in the declared history: clearing the later PR 200 panel session's prior list still validates but leaves `crossRoundRepetitions` at 1. Resolve each session's declared ancestors and compare only against findings in those sessions.
findings.failureMode: A valid corpus with independent or non-array-ordered sessions reports incorrect declared-history repetition metrics.
findings.title: Compute repetitions from declared predecessors

findings.description: This verifies only that each `priorSessionIds` target exists after all session IDs have been collected. Self-references, forward-reference cycles, and multi-session cycles therefore pass validation; a PR 200 session with itself as its sole prior is accepted. Traverse the declared history graph (or require a valid topological order) and reject self/cyclic ancestry so the corpus cannot claim an impossible review history.
findings.failureMode: A corpus with cyclic declared session ancestry is accepted as valid, invalidating any history-based calibration or repetition interpretation.
findings.title: Reject cycles in declared session history

findings.description: The fixture declares `context.input.baseSha` as `runtimeProvenanceField` and copies that value into every `executingRuntimeSha`, but production ingestion defines `baseSha` as GitHub's `merge_base_commit.sha`, the commit against which the PR diff is computed rather than the revision of the deployed process. Whenever the panel service is deployed from a revision other than that merge base (including ordinary deployment lag), `eval:continuity` and the default metrics output report false runtime provenance and can incorrectly conclude that all rounds shared one runtime. Capture an actual build/deployment SHA from the running service and use that provenance instead.
findings.failureMode: A review run executes on deployment D while the PR's merge base is B; the frozen AC-7 report emits B as `executingRuntimeSha`, producing wrong provenance and a false shared-runtime result.
findings.title: Do not label the PR merge base as the executing runtime

findings.description: The fixture declares `context.input.baseSha` as `runtimeProvenanceField` and uses that value as every `executingRuntimeSha`, but panel input `baseSha` is populated from GitHub's comparison `merge_base_commit.sha`, not from the executing deployment. If studio2 runs a different revision from the PR's merge base, `eval:continuity` reports the merge base as the runtime and falsely collapses runs under that SHA, so AC-7/runtime-provenance output is wrong. Capture an actual deployment/build SHA from the run record instead of relabeling `baseSha`.
findings.failureMode: A panel run executes deployment R while reviewing a PR whose merge base is B; the continuity report outputs B as executingRuntimeSha and produces incorrect runtime-provenance grouping.
findings.title: Do not treat PR merge-base SHA as runtime provenance

findings.description: This new percentage helper rounds exact half-ties with `Math.round`, while both existing golden-metrics implementations deliberately use round-half-to-even. For example, a valid 1-of-16 blocking calibration is emitted as 6.3% here but as 6.2% everywhere else, so continuity metrics disagree with the evaluator's published rounding rule on boundary inputs. Reuse the established half-even calculation.
findings.failureMode: A valid continuity fixture has a rate whose one-decimal percentage is exactly halfway, such as 1 accepted blocking appearance out of 16; continuity reports 6.3% instead of the canonical 6.2%.
findings.title: Use the evaluator's established tie rounding

findings.description: The fixture declares `context.input.baseSha` as `runtimeProvenanceField` and copies that value into every `executingRuntimeSha`, but panel ingestion sets `baseSha` from `compareCommitsWithBasehead(...).merge_base_commit.sha`. On any review executed by a deployment whose revision differs from the PR merge base, `eval:continuity` and `eval:metrics` therefore report the merge base as the executing runtime and falsely satisfy the runtime-provenance metric. Capture a revision emitted by the running deployment instead of deriving this field from `baseSha`.
findings.failureMode: For a panel run whose deployed runtime commit differs from the pull request merge base, the continuity report emits the merge-base SHA as `executingRuntimeSha`, yielding incorrect AC-7 provenance.
findings.title: Do not label the merge base as the executing runtime

findings.description: `loadContinuityFixture(path)` treats caller-selected JSON as a continuity fixture, but `assertFixture` never validates `postDeployValidation` before this line publishes it. A fixture with that property removed exits 0 and `JSON.stringify` silently omits `postDeployValidation`, so the evaluator produces a successful report without the explicitly required unvalidated/deployment observation. Validate the required status, reason, observations, counts, and runtime SHAs at the JSON boundary before emitting the report.
findings.failureMode: Running `evals/golden/continuity.mjs <fixture>` on a fixture missing `postDeployValidation` succeeds and returns a report with no post-deploy status instead of rejecting the unsupported fixture.
findings.title: Reject fixtures that omit post-deploy validation

findings.description: With `PANEL_JUDGE_HARNESS=claude` (or `codex`), `PANEL_JUDGE_FALLBACK_HARNESS=native`, and no `PANEL_JUDGE_NATIVE_MODEL`, the server defaults the native lane to `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`, but this evaluator leaves `nativeModel` undefined because it tests only the primary. If the primary fails, `generateAdjudication` reaches the native fallback without a model, its target rejects the empty id, and the golden/fidelity run fails instead of exercising the same production policy. Base this default on either the primary or fallback being native.
findings.failureMode: A supported custom primary with native fallback succeeds in production configuration but golden evaluation reports a failed judge when the primary lane fails.
findings.title: Default the model for a native fallback

findings.description: The server applies the Sol default only when `PANEL_JUDGE_NATIVE_MODEL` is absent and rejects explicit invalid values, but the changed evaluator expressions turn a blank value into the default and let other malformed values (for example `google/model` or `openai`) reach `generateAdjudication`. A blank override can therefore run Sol, while a malformed native attempt can be classified as a lane error and return an `ok` result from Codex, even though production cannot start under either configuration. Parse and validate any explicit provider/model override up front in both `productionModel` and `productionJudge`; default only when the variable is actually undefined.
findings.failureMode: Golden evaluation succeeds under an explicit native-model environment that the production service rejects at startup, so the stored result does not represent a runnable production policy.
findings.title: Reject invalid native-model overrides before fallback

findings.description: After changing the evaluator's implicit primary to `native`, setting only `PANEL_JUDGE_FALLBACK_HARNESS=native` creates two identical native lanes here. The server rejects that exact configuration at startup, but `productionJudge` passes it to `generateAdjudication`, which can return a successful evaluation from the first native call (or retry the same route as a fake fallback). Add the same primary/fallback equality validation used by `factory-host` before running the evaluator.
findings.failureMode: Golden or fidelity output is produced for a duplicate-lane judge configuration that production refuses, and a native failure is retried through the same route rather than failing configuration.
findings.title: Reject a fallback that equals the default native judge

findings.description: AxGEPA prefers `scoreVectors[index]` whenever it is present, so the adjacent per-row `scores` values are never used. A candidate can keep the one expected must-fix family while returning the wrong factual state, causal relation, severity, disposition, or history for every non-blocker; `mustFixPrecision` and `acceptedBlockerRetention` both remain 1, and this adapter presents every row as perfect despite `row.ok` being false. Put the per-case, per-field correctness values into each `scoreVectors` entry so Ax ranks the classifications it is meant to optimize.
findings.failureMode: During the normal Ax optimization path, a candidate that preserves the blocker but misclassifies all non-blocking/dismissed cases receives perfect vectors and can be selected/certified as correct.
findings.title: Include classification correctness in Ax score vectors

findings.description: `loadKnownAnswers` returns `ordering-non-blocking` with `calibration.status === 'excluded'`, but this map scores every case without consulting that status. Consequently, reporting this invalid historical control as must-fix lowers `mustFixPrecision` from 1 to 0.5 and sends its failure into optimizer reflection, so the calibration signal includes evidence the corpus explicitly says to exclude. Filter calibration-ineligible cases before constructing scored rows and aggregate metrics; retain the excluded case only in non-calibration regression checks.
findings.failureMode: The standard four-case scoring path penalizes and reflects on the excluded job-selection control, producing a different candidate ranking/training signal than the declared calibration cohort.
findings.title: Exclude the invalid control from calibration scores

findings.description: `acceptedBlockerRetention` is encoded as an ordinary score-vector dimension, but AxGEPA Pareto-ranks all dimensions rather than enforcing any one as mandatory. Starting from a candidate that reports no must-fixes yields `(precision=1, retention=0)`; after a noisy blocker-retaining candidate is accepted, Ax returns both vectors in its Pareto front because neither dominates the other. Reject blocker-dropping evaluations before they enter Ax's archive so every returned candidate satisfies the declared hard constraint.
findings.failureMode: A normal optimization run can return a Pareto candidate that omitted an accepted must-fix, despite accepted-blocker retention being declared a hard constraint.
findings.title: Reject blocker-dropping candidates before Pareto ranking

findings.description: Unlike the panel path, this only validates Open SWE findings that were manually listed; it never compares `session.findings` with all finding-marked review comments belonging to a calibrated review. Deleting a valid 🟡 finding from a session still passes validation, so the system's accepted/reported family inventory and precision can silently omit a real review output. Build the expected Open SWE finding inventory from the frozen comment artifacts and require a one-to-one match before scoring.
findings.failureMode: An omitted Open SWE review finding passes validation and is absent from the published calibration counts.
findings.title: Require exhaustive Open SWE finding extraction

findings.description: The exhaustive panel inventory is built only from `mustFix` and `waived`, but the production result publishes non-waived plausible (and confirmed below-threshold) adjudications as non-blocking findings. A calibrated session cannot list one of those outputs because `panelBindingComplete` then sees an extra session finding, while omitting it makes `validNonBlockingPreservation` miss the output entirely. Include the record's published non-blocking adjudications in `panelRows` with `blocking: false`, deduplicated from must-fix/waived rows.
findings.failureMode: A panel non-blocking finding is either rejected from the session or omitted from non-blocking preservation metrics.
findings.title: Include adjudicated non-blocking panel findings

findings.description: The session check binds its top-level review artifact to `session.reviewId`, but this Open SWE branch never requires a finding's source comment to have that same `reviewId`. A genuine yellow comment from a later review can be added to an earlier session and passes validation, attributing the finding to the wrong reviewed head/phase and corrupting phase overlap and history metrics. Require `source.reviewId === session.reviewId` for finding-source comments (while still allowing separately identified reply artifacts as disposition evidence).
findings.failureMode: A source-backed finding comment from another review is accepted under the wrong session and reviewed head.
findings.title: Bind Open SWE finding comments to the session review

findings.description: `result.waived` rows have shape `{ finding, reason, basis? }`, but this spreads the wrapper as though it were a finding. Their `fingerprint` and `severity` therefore read as undefined, so a valid development-calibration session containing any waived finding fails the inventory/drift checks even when its extraction is exact. Map `mustFix` directly and map each waived row from `row.finding` while setting `blocking: false`.
findings.failureMode: A valid calibrated panel record containing a waived finding is rejected by the corpus validator.
findings.title: Unwrap waived findings before panel binding

findings.description: The source-backed comparison only includes `review` and `review-comment` artifacts, so the `operator-disposition` artifacts that decide each family's factual and delivery labels are never checked against the frozen `:issue-comments` response. If an extracted disposition body/author/URL is edited or fabricated and its local content hash is recomputed, validation still succeeds and `computeAdjudicationMetrics` publishes calibration based on a disposition absent from the authoritative GitHub bytes. Project issue comments too and require every operator-disposition artifact to match its raw comment.
findings.failureMode: A rehashed fabricated operator disposition passes validation and yields unsupported precision/disposition metrics.
findings.title: Bind operator dispositions to raw issue comments

findings.description: The family validator only checks that `dispositionSourceArtifactId` names some artifact; it does not require that artifact's calibration status be `disposition-evidence` or even that it appear in the family's evidence inventory. A family can therefore cite its original model finding (or an unrelated artifact) as the alleged operator disposition and still contribute hand-authored factual/delivery labels to precision. Require the referenced artifact to be disposition evidence and to be included in `evidenceArtifactIds`.
findings.failureMode: A calibrated family with no cited disposition evidence is accepted and changes the reported precision/disposition results.
findings.title: Require an actual disposition-evidence source

findings.description: This checks only that the hand-authored `record.source` SHAs look like SHAs; it never compares the record's PR number, repository, base/head/merge SHAs, or merged timestamp with the frozen `github:<pr>:pull` bytes. A record can therefore be relabeled to another syntactically valid head or PR while retaining unrelated raw source evidence and still pass, making the reported source interval and provenance false. Project the canonical source fields from the raw pull response and compare them before accepting the record.
findings.failureMode: A rehashed record with source metadata that disagrees with its authoritative pull payload is accepted as a valid corpus record.
findings.title: Bind record provenance to the frozen pull response

findings.description: The CLI never checks that `--report`, `--ledger`, and `--plan` resolve to distinct files, and this unconditional `writeFile` runs only after the ledger has been closed. With `--report` equal (or symlinked) to the ledger path, a successful five-call run replaces the entire append-only ledger with the summary report; with `--report` equal to the plan path it destroys the registered plan. Resolve/canonicalize all three paths and reject aliases before executing any provider call.
findings.failureMode: A successful live CLI invocation with `--report` aliased to `--ledger` or `--plan` irreversibly overwrites the audit ledger or registered plan.
findings.title: Reject aliased output paths before the live run

findings.description: The interruption check only detects an intent with no terminal. There is another crash window after a successful terminal is appended but before `AdjudicationAdapter` appends its replayable `adjudication`/proposal row. Retrying that ledger sees neither `failed` nor `incomplete`, repeats the already completed provider request, and then `report()` counts both terminals. Reproducing a ledger cut immediately after the first terminal caused five new calls and a completed report with six calls. Detect this unmatched terminal/cache state and refuse the retry rather than duplicating spend and accounting.
findings.failureMode: A process kill between the terminal and adapter cache append allows an in-place retry to duplicate a paid request and overcount the completed run.
findings.title: Treat terminal-without-cache as an interrupted run

findings.description: The completed-ledger check occurs only after `AxGEPA.compile`. If a completed ledger is damaged by losing one cached `adjudication`/proposal row while retaining `micro-pilot-result`, the adapter misses the cache and invokes the live harness before this line notices `calls.cursor !== 0`. A reproduced replay made one provider call and mutated the supposedly immutable ledger before throwing `replay-divergence`. Verify that every planned replay key/result is present and consistent before constructing/compiling the adapter, so damaged completed ledgers fail without credentials or spend.
findings.failureMode: Replaying a completed but partially damaged ledger unexpectedly performs paid provider calls and appends new rows before failing.
findings.title: Validate completed replay inventory before compiling

findings.description: The new CLI records only `git rev-parse HEAD`; unlike the existing pilot, it never checks `git status --porcelain`. If a developer has modified the pilot, corpus, or prompts locally, dry-run stamps that uncommitted content with the clean HEAD SHA, and live mode can reconstruct the same dirty plan and spend provider calls while the resulting ledger falsely attributes the execution to HEAD. Reuse the clean-clone revision check before building/reconstructing either mode.
findings.failureMode: Running the dry or live micro-pilot from a dirty checkout produces audit evidence and provider spend attributed to a commit that does not contain the executed inputs/code.
findings.title: Refuse dirty source before attributing the run to HEAD

findings.description: A completed replay compares only the reconstructed Ax result and then returns the previously stored report verbatim; it never verifies the intent/terminal telemetry that report claims to summarize. Changing a successful terminal's `usage.total` from 2 to 999999 still returned `replay: true` and `totalTokens: 10` while the ledger terminals totaled 1,000,007. Recompute the report from the ledger and fail replay if it differs from the stored report (and validate the terminal/request hashes) instead of accepting stale accounting.
findings.failureMode: A completed ledger with corrupted or edited telemetry is accepted as a successful replay and reports accounting that contradicts the ledger.
findings.title: Recompute the report when validating completed replay

findings.description: The early `failed-ledger` refusal is caught by this generic block, and because `prior` is absent and the ledger is nonempty, the block appends another `micro-pilot-failure`. Retrying the committed four-row failed ledger was correctly refused but changed its hash and grew it to five rows. Exclude pre-existing-ledger refusal paths from failure journaling (or decide whether to append before opening the existing artifact) so inspecting/retrying immutable evidence cannot modify it.
findings.failureMode: Attempting to retry a failed ledger mutates the immutable failure evidence even though no run is allowed.
findings.title: Keep failed-ledger retry refusal byte-preserving

findings.description: The telemetry guard checks only that each counter is nonnegative and finite; it never checks the normalized accounting invariant `total === input + cached + cacheCreation + output` (with reasoning already included in output). A harness result with 10 input and 5 output tokens but `total: 0` is accepted for all five calls and produces a successful report claiming zero tokens. Validate the arithmetic before writing a successful terminal so the unit-cost report cannot silently undercount malformed vendor telemetry.
findings.failureMode: Malformed or inconsistent provider usage is accepted and the completed micro-pilot reports the wrong token cost.
findings.title: Reject internally inconsistent usage totals

findings.description: The pairwise parser accepts any truthy next token as a path, including another flag. For example, `adjudication-pilot.mjs --dry-run --plan` succeeds and writes the generated plan to a file literally named `--plan` instead of rejecting the missing dry-run path; similarly a missing live value can redirect the report to a flag-named file after provider spend. Reject values beginning with `--` (as the existing pilot parser does) before performing any write or call.
findings.failureMode: A malformed CLI invocation with a missing path is treated as successful and writes its artifact to an unintended flag-named file.
findings.title: Do not consume another option as a path value

findings.description: All previous-key rows are rewritten in the same transaction after `oauth.refreshToken` has already rotated the selected credential at the provider. If the UPDATE for any shadowed lower-priority row then fails, the catch rolls the whole transaction back, including the selected row's new refresh token; the provider has invalidated the old token, so the shared credential is permanently lost. Rewrite opportunistic shadow rows before performing the external refresh or in separate transactions so their failure cannot roll back a newly rotated token.
findings.failureMode: With an expired selected OAuth row and any shadowed previous-key row, a DB failure on the shadow-row UPDATE after a successful rotating refresh leaves the database holding the now-invalid old refresh token.
findings.title: Do not couple shadow-row rewrites to token refresh

findings.description: The new automation audience chooses any org-scoped credential before the fallback user's row, but every native provider is OAuth-only (`claude-max` rejects `api_key`, while xAI and Codex require `get(...).type === 'oauth'`). Thus a valid, common Factory setup with an org API key plus the configured user's OAuth login now makes real golden lanes fail authentication instead of using the fallback OAuth row. Make automation resolution OAuth-aware for these native consumers; the same incompatible construction is duplicated in `ensemble.mjs`, `match.mjs`, and `optimize/pilot.mjs`.
findings.failureMode: When an organization has a shared API key for anthropic/xai/openai-codex and the configured user has OAuth, every affected golden native entry point selects the org key and then fails before issuing the model request.
findings.title: Do not let org API keys shadow native OAuth

findings.description: A previous-key row in the losing scope makes every otherwise-valid credential read enter `refreshLocked`, and this UPDATE is allowed to fail the whole call. For example, with a current-key org API credential and an old-key shadowed user row, a transient write error or a read-only credential role causes `getApiKey` to throw instead of returning the valid org key. Since shadow rotation is opportunistic, perform it best-effort/outside the selected credential's access transaction rather than making its write success a prerequisite for serving the winner.
findings.failureMode: During key rotation, a write failure on a lower-priority row turns a valid selected credential into an authentication outage.
findings.title: Keep shadow-key rotation off the credential read path

findings.description: This call omits `oauth` because the unlocked row was an API key. If another writer replaces it with an expired-but-refreshable OAuth credential before the lock, `refreshLocked` sees OAuth but rolls back at `if (!oauth)` and leaves no snapshot. The native xAI/Codex wrappers then reject the request as not logged in even though the committed OAuth row has a usable refresh token. Always resolve/pass the provider for the locked row rather than basing it on the stale pre-lock type.
findings.failureMode: A concurrent API-key-to-OAuth login between the initial read and row lock makes one xAI or Codex native request fail authentication despite a refreshable committed OAuth credential.
findings.title: Pass the OAuth provider into rewrite transactions

findings.description: The host manifest advances code-sdk, core, Factory, and pg in a feature PR despite the hard rule that upstream bumps must be standalone gated PRs. The existing contract-test gate means the bootstrap exception does not apply, so this change is not mergeable as authored; move these version changes (and the mastra devDependency bump at line 32) to a version-bump PR.
findings.failureMode: The required review/merge process rejects a feature change that bundles host upstream-version upgrades.
findings.title: Split host dependency bumps from this feature PR

findings.description: This feature PR changes the contract-test pins for code-sdk, core, and Factory even though the repository's hard rule requires upstream version bumps to be standalone PRs gated by contract-tests. This is not the bootstrap exception—the dependency gates already existed—so the PR is not mergeable under the repository operating contract until these bump lines are reverted or moved to their own version-bump PR.
findings.failureMode: The required review/merge process rejects a feature change that also advances upstream package pins.
findings.title: Split upstream bumps from this feature PR

findings.description: These development pins advance code-sdk and Factory in a feature PR, contrary to the mandatory standalone version-bump process. The Factory contract-test gate predates this PR, so the bootstrap exception is unavailable; revert these pin changes here and land the cohort in its own gated bump PR.
findings.failureMode: The required review/merge process rejects a factory-glue feature change containing upstream pin upgrades.
findings.title: Split factory-glue dependency bumps from this feature PR

findings.description: The harness manifest advances code-sdk and core in a feature PR although the repository contract requires upstream bumps to land separately behind contract-tests. Because those gates already exist, this is not a bootstrap alignment and blocks the prescribed merge process until moved to a dedicated bump PR.
findings.failureMode: The required review/merge process rejects a harness feature change containing upstream pin upgrades.
findings.title: Split harness dependency bumps from this feature PR

findings.description: This changes the sandbox package's upstream core pin in a credentials feature PR, violating the mandatory rule that upstream version bumps are standalone contract-tested PRs. The core gate already existed, so the bootstrap exception does not apply; keep this package on its prior pin until a dedicated bump PR lands.
findings.failureMode: The required review/merge process rejects a sandbox package version bump embedded in a feature PR.
findings.title: Split sandbox core bump from this feature PR

findings.description: This only verifies that `src/job-selection.js` has no label, which is exactly how `scoreRun` continues to treat the file as a negative control.
