A run containing the demonstrated line-3 ordering finding makes zero judge calls but is still counted as one unmatched finding, producing strict precision 0 and feedback that presents the valid defect as unmatched. No exclusion metadata or scorer handling exists at this head, so the test/history changes do not quarantine the invalid control from current scoring. Add exact tag/file exclusion metadata and remove matching findings before candidate generation, metrics, and feedback, with a scorer-boundary test.
findings.failureMode: Scoring fixture 287 with a finding for the real job-selection ordering change still reports that valid finding as a false positive and lowers benchmark precision/score.
findings.title: Quarantine the finding at the scorer boundary

findings.description: `reported` trusts free-floating family IDs from candidate decisions instead of binding each disposition to its corresponding case. If the true blocker row is changed to `non-blocking` while a clean row is returned as that blocker family with `must-fix`, `acceptedBlockersRetained` remains true and `mustFixPrecision` remains 1; the adapter therefore rewards correct rows even though the actual blocker was lost and a false blocker was emitted. Derive reported/accepted families from identity-matched case-decision pairs (using the input family's identity), preserving any intended family-level deduplication.
findings.failureMode: An adjudicator loses the actual accepted blocker and copies its family ID onto a clean case, so both the hard retention gate and must-fix precision pass.
findings.title: Bind blocker metrics to the corresponding case rows

findings.description: Both replay paths test the cached value's truthiness rather than whether the replay key exists. A completed adjudication or proposal whose recorded result is `null`, `false`, `0`, or an empty string is therefore ignored on the next identical evaluation and the injected provider is called again. In particular, `scoreAdjudications` deliberately treats `null` as a contract failure, so that malformed adjudicator result is reachable; a retry can return a different decision and change the score instead of deterministically replaying the append-only ledger. Use `ledger.cached.has(key)` (and then `get`) at both sites.
findings.failureMode: A malformed/falsy provider result is journaled as complete, but an identical replay makes another provider call and can produce a different optimizer result.
findings.title: Replay cached falsy results instead of invoking providers again

findings.description: For `repeated-unchanged`, the loader merely requires the case-authored `evidenceChanged` flag to equal `false`; it never compares the prior and current evidence. Changing the repeat case to an entirely different diff still loads with `evidenceChanged: false`, so the scorer accepts `repeated-unchanged` and trains the optimizer to dismiss a finding even though its evidence changed. Compare the prior/current diff, context, and source evidence (or a canonical evidence hash) before accepting this history state.
findings.failureMode: A repeat fixture with materially changed diff/evidence is accepted as unchanged, yielding an incorrect history label and optimizer score.
findings.title: Recompute unchanged-history evidence instead of trusting its flag

findings.description: The history check only compares the referenced case's family/fingerprint and `evidenceChanged`; it does not require the referenced case to be distinct or to belong to a prior session declared by the current corpus session. A repeated case can point to itself (with its own fingerprint) and still load, fabricating the history evidence used to score `repeated-unchanged`. Resolve both cases' sessions and require the prior case's session to be an ancestor in `session.priorSessionIds` (which the corpus records for the real 5036180576 transition).
findings.failureMode: A self-referential or later-session history pointer passes validation, so the optimizer is trained/scored on a falsely repeated finding.
findings.title: Validate history against the corpus session graph

findings.description: The source-selector check binds family, finding, fingerprint, session, and head, but never checks `value.input.pullRequest` against the manifest/source record. A case file can therefore claim PR 199 while selecting a PR 200 session and still load successfully after its manifest hash is updated. `assertPrIsolation` then partitions that case under the false PR number, allowing rows from the same source PR to cross train/validation folds and contaminating evaluation. Reject cases whose input pull request does not equal the selected record's pull request.
findings.failureMode: A mislabeled known-answer case passes source validation and causes cases from one actual PR to be treated as different PRs during fold-isolation checks.
findings.title: Bind each case's pull request to its source record

findings.description: The loader accepts any file listed in the selected panel record as `value.source.file`; it verifies that file's oid/hash but never checks that its path is the panel finding's `file`/affected location. A hunk-metadata case can therefore be changed to bind its finding to `package.json` and still load, and the unrelated file is then supplied to the adjudicator as source evidence. Require the source-file path to match the selected finding's anchored file before accepting its historical oid/hash.
findings.failureMode: A known-answer case passes hash/source validation while pairing a finding with an unrelated changed file, so adjudication and calibration run against false evidence.
findings.title: Require source-file evidence to match the finding anchor

findings.description: The job-replacement entry records 11 deletions and `@@ -1,13 +1,5 @@`, but its patch body has 9 removed lines and 11 old-side lines; the same mismatch affects job-selection and both provider entries, in both the per-file patches and aggregate diff. Reverse-applying the aggregate diff to the supplied post-images fails with `error: corrupt patch at line 35`, so the frozen input cannot reconstruct its before modules and any rerun reviews malformed metadata instead of the intended six executable cases. Correct all four counts/ranges and validate application against repositoryContent.
findings.failureMode: Loading tag 287 and reverse-applying its aggregate diff to the supplied post-images exits 128 as a corrupt patch, invalidating the retained experiment input.
findings.title: Frozen patches contain invalid hunk and deletion counts

findings.description: The report says baseline/candidate hits were 27/27 and 26/27, precision fell from 0.9643 to 0.8667, and five gates failed. The PR's final reset record says the corrected-input rerun was 25/27 to 27/27 with precision 0.8333 to 0.9643 and only the cross-provider gain condition failed. Thus the durable report preserves the superseded outcome and wrong failure rationale; an operator auditing or extending MASTRA-287 will use incorrect measurements even though the no-promotion decision happens to remain unchanged. Replace the results and gate table with the corrected rerun.
findings.failureMode: A maintainer uses the committed experiment report as the durable result and concludes the candidate regressed and generated more false positives, when the final reset run actually improved both metrics and failed only the provider-diversity gate.
findings.title: Committed report records the invalidated run instead of the reset result

findings.description: The behavior cases define `read`, `before`/`after`, and provider transforms locally rather than reconstructing them from `fixture.input.files`; the direct test run therefore reports all four tests passing even though the retained aggregate diff is not applicable to `repositoryContent`. Edits or corruption in the actual lane input do not affect these assertions, so CI can certify a different behavior than reruns review. Reconstruct the recorded before/after modules, assert the generated post-images and aggregate/per-file patch agreement, and execute those modules.
findings.failureMode: A tag-287 patch or repositoryContent entry drifts from the hand-coded examples; CI remains green, but subsequent evaluation runs no longer reproduce the behavior the test/report says was frozen.
findings.title: Behavior checks execute hand-written copies instead of the fixture

findings.description: The fixture declares `context.input.baseSha` to be its runtime-provenance field and copies that value into every `executingRuntimeSha`. On the production GitHub panel path, however, `baseSha` is explicitly populated from `comparison.data.merge_base_commit.sha` and merely passed through to the panel snapshot; it identifies the PR evidence base, not the code revision executing the service. Consequently both new eval commands publish a sole runtime SHA and claim AC-7 provenance that the stored records cannot establish. Populate `executingRuntimeSha` from an authoritative deployment/runtime-revision source, and do not emit the runtime metric when that source is unavailable.
findings.failureMode: `pnpm eval:continuity` reports `cfaf29...` as the sole executing runtime for all 13 rounds even though the fixture's cited source only records each PR's merge base, producing a false mainline evaluation result.
findings.title: Do not relabel the merge base as runtime provenance

findings.description: When scoreVectors are present, Ax uses those vectors instead of the parallel scores array. This adapter's vectors contain only must-fix precision and blocker retention, so factual, causal, severity, history, and ordinary disposition failures never affect optimization. A batch where every row fails those fields but preserves must-fix dispositions returns perfect vectors for every row. Include per-case/axis correctness in scoreVectors or omit scoreVectors so the zero scores are honored.
findings.failureMode: An adjudicator gets all classification axes wrong while preserving family IDs and must-fix dispositions; adapter outputs scores all zero but vectors all perfect, and Ax ranks the candidate as perfect.
findings.title: Ax ignores all per-case correctness scores

findings.description: scoreAdjudications maps every loaded case without checking calibration.status. The standard known-answer batch contains ordering-non-blocking with status excluded and the source reason says to exclude it from calibration, so that row can produce failures and alter precision/optimizer feedback. Filter excluded rows before calibration scoring while retaining them only for non-calibration regression checks.
findings.failureMode: Calling scoreAdjudications or AdjudicationAdapter.evaluate on loadKnownAnswers() includes ordering-non-blocking in calibration despite its excluded status, corrupting the calibration result.
findings.title: Excluded case is still scored

findings.description: acceptedBlockerRetention is emitted as one ordinary Pareto objective. Ax can trade or tie a zero on that objective against precision or other objectives, so a candidate that drops the known must-fix hunk still receives nonzero aggregate fitness and can remain/select on the Pareto front. Enforce retention by zeroing/rejecting the entire candidate when false rather than exposing it as a tradeable dimension.
findings.failureMode: A candidate downgrades hunk-metadata-must-fix to non-blocking; the adapter returns vectors {mustFixPrecision:1, acceptedBlockerRetention:0}, which scalarize to nonzero fitness instead of failing the declared hard constraint.
findings.title: Blocker retention is not a hard constraint

findings.description: The full row.input passed to adjudicate includes case IDs such as manifest-refuted, ordering-non-blocking, hunk-metadata-must-fix, and manifest-repeat-dismissed. These values directly disclose expected factual, disposition, and history labels even though assertInputIsolation only blocks label-shaped keys. An adjudicator can branch on the IDs and score well without adjudicating the evidence, invalidating optimizer results. Use opaque IDs in model-visible input or attach internal IDs after adjudication.
findings.failureMode: A candidate reads label words from input.caseId and returns the indicated expected states, producing inflated known-answer scores without reasoning over the finding evidence.
findings.title: Label-bearing case IDs reach the adjudicator

findings.description: When reported.size is zero the scorer returns precision 1, unlike the existing corpus metric which marks a zero denominator unvalidated/null. Thus a candidate that reports no must-fix findings is rewarded with perfect precision; in blocker-free/minibatch slices this also combines with vacuous retention for a perfect safety vector. Return an unvalidated/no-credit value rather than 1 for a zero denominator.
findings.failureMode: On an evaluation batch with no reported must-fix decisions, mustFixPrecision is 1 even though precision is not estimable, inflating the optimizer objective and favoring silence.
findings.title: Silence receives perfect must-fix precision

findings.description: A lane's existing `normalizeUsage` returns a non-null object for any nonempty usage payload and fills absent token categories with zero. For example, a valid review accompanied by `{prompt_tokens: 10}` yields a non-null lane usage even though output usage is unavailable; this new check then publishes `usage.complete: true`. Downstream baseline totals consequently present an undercount as complete. Completeness must be carried from validation of all required usage components (or the lane normalizer must reject partial payloads), not inferred solely from non-nullness.
findings.failureMode: A provider response contains only partial token usage; the ensemble records the resulting lower bound as complete, causing evaluator and baseline usage totals to be trusted as exact.
findings.title: Do not equate non-null lane usage with completeness

findings.description: For the current detailed SDK shape, an explicit `noCacheTokens` value wins even when it contradicts `inputTokens`. A response such as `inputTokens: 3`, details `{noCacheTokens: 3, cacheReadTokens: 2}`, and `outputTokens: 1` is normalized to five input tokens and returned as complete when `totalTokens` is absent, despite the provider's total input being three. Check that a present total input equals no-cache plus read/write cache tokens before accepting the usage.
findings.failureMode: A provider supplies internally inconsistent detailed input usage without totalTokens; decision provenance inflates the known usage and marks the impossible breakdown complete.
findings.title: Validate detailed input decomposition

findings.description: The detailed-usage branch validates integer values and the overall total but never verifies that reasoning tokens are a subset of output tokens. With `outputTokens: 1`, `outputTokenDetails.reasoningTokens: 2`, and an otherwise consistent total, the function returns an impossible `reasoning: 2` record and aggregation labels it complete. Reject usage where reasoning exceeds output before returning it.
findings.failureMode: A malformed provider usage response reports more reasoning than output tokens; evaluator provenance publishes the impossible reasoning count as complete instead of marking usage unknown.
findings.title: Reject reasoning counts above total output

findings.description: When the judge harnesses actually run and then all fail, `JudgeAttemptFailure` preserves their attempts, but this branch writes `judgePromptHash: null` even though the shared instruction `prompt` is known and was used to build every attempt. This makes a failed ensemble internally inconsistent (`judgeProvenance.attempts` is populated while its known instruction-version hash is missing), and an all-failed baseline cannot identify which judge instructions produced those attempts. Emit `hash(prompt)` here just as on the successful path.
findings.failureMode: All judge routes fail after invocation; the emitted evaluation record drops the known shared judge prompt hash and downstream baseline provenance reports null despite recorded judge attempts.
findings.title: Keep the known judge instruction hash on failed attempts

findings.description: Each attempt is restricted to safe integers, but `addUsage` adds them without checking that the aggregate remains safe. For example, combining one attempt at `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` with another at 2 rounds the mathematical sum 9,007,199,254,740,993 down to 9,007,199,254,740,992 while `aggregateGenerationUsage` reports `status: 'complete'`. Detect unsafe accumulation and mark the aggregate incomplete/invalid rather than publishing imprecise totals.
findings.failureMode: Multiple untrusted provider usage records are individually safe but their sum is unsafe, causing a complete provenance aggregate with a rounded token total.
findings.title: Guard aggregate token sums from overflow

findings.description: `aggregateGenerationUsage` is a new exported abstraction, but the production tree has only one real call site (`runGenerationWithFallback`; the other references are tests). This violates the repository's hard rule that every new abstraction have at least two real call sites, so the change is not mergeable under the repository operating contract. Inline it into its sole consumer or add a second actual consumer.
findings.failureMode: The feature reaches review with a new abstraction that has only one production consumer, causing the repository's mandatory delivery gate to reject the change.
findings.title: Avoid a one-consumer usage abstraction

findings.description: `reported` trusts any must-fix row's claimed `familyId` without pairing it to the case being scored. On the committed calibration batch, a candidate can mark the real hunk-metadata blocker non-blocking, then put that blocker family ID on either dismissed manifest case; `acceptedBlockersRetained` remains true and the unchanged dismissed row still receives nonzero optimizer objectives. Thus the advertised hard constraint can be bypassed by a wrong-family decision and Ax can rank a candidate that lost the accepted blocker. Compute reported blockers from case/decision pairs only when the case and family IDs match (and the decision is contract-valid).
findings.failureMode: A candidate moves an accepted blocker's family ID onto an unrelated case while downgrading the actual blocker, but receives retention and precision scores of 1 instead of having every objective zeroed.
findings.title: Bind blocker retention to the decision's own case

findings.description: The replay branch tests the cached value's truthiness rather than whether the replay key exists (and the proposal path repeats this at line 18). A completed malformed adjudication such as `null` is deliberately scoreable as a contract failure and is stored by `Ledger.append`, but evaluating the same fixture/candidate again invokes `adjudicate` and appends another row instead of replaying it; a nondeterministic retry can therefore change that candidate's score and breaks selective replay. Check `cached.has(key)` and then return/get the stored value at both sites.
findings.failureMode: A completed falsy adjudicator or proposer result is treated as a cache miss, causing duplicate external calls and non-reproducible scores/proposals.
findings.title: Use key presence when replaying completed results

findings.description: `roundFingerprints` is recreated for every run, so this check only detects duplicate fingerprints inside one round. The frozen fixture repeats fingerprint `v1:7cfad00d…` in rounds 8 and 9, yet the mainline evaluator reports `exactFingerprintDuplicates: 0`; maintain a fixture-wide fingerprint set so the continuity output reports the cross-round duplicate instead of understating exact repetition.
findings.failureMode: Running `pnpm eval:continuity` on the bundled PR 195 fixture emits an incorrect exact duplicate count of 0 even though the same full fingerprint occurs in two rounds.
findings.title: Count exact fingerprints across rounds

findings.description: This exposes the new report only as a separate `eval:continuity` command; the unchanged `eval:metrics` command still runs only `metrics.mjs`, which neither imports nor emits continuity data. Consequently the default optimizer-facing metrics output omits all PR 195 continuity, duplicate-rate, and calibration fields. Wire `computeContinuityMetrics` into the default metrics builder/output rather than leaving the new slice on a side command only.
findings.failureMode: Running the repository's default `pnpm eval:metrics` entry point after this change produces only the existing Phase-A/AC-4 arms and no continuity metrics.
findings.title: Include continuity in the default metrics command

findings.description: The panel appearances classify the replay defect as `authoritative-replay`, but Open SWE thread `f_1e3c68f4ef` is stored as `pending-authoritative-replay`. These are the single shared defect from the PR's continuity comparison (the thread reviews head `8579…`, where the panel also reports this replay family, and both resolve at `2864…`), so set the thread's family to the same canonical ID. As written, a panel/Open-SWE family intersection reports zero shared defects and overcounts distinct families.
findings.failureMode: Any comparison of the bundled panel and Open SWE family sets returns an empty intersection instead of the documented one shared authoritative-replay defect.
findings.title: Use one family ID for the shared replay defect

findings.description: The unknown-family guard reads a normal object's prototype chain. A custom fixture with `families: {}` and an appearance whose family is `toString` passes validation, after which the evaluator counts one accepted family against zero real families. Check an own property (for example with `Object.hasOwn`) so malformed fixture family IDs cannot produce valid-looking continuity metrics.
findings.failureMode: Invoking the supported evaluator with a malformed fixture that names an Object prototype property emits incorrect metrics instead of rejecting the unknown family.
findings.title: Reject inherited family names

findings.description: The fixture declares `context.input.baseSha` to be its runtime-provenance field and copies it into every `executingRuntimeSha`, but the production evidence path populates `baseSha` from GitHub's `merge_base_commit.sha`. That identifies the revision used for the PR comparison, not the deployed process; the repository's earlier eval pinning records a deployed commit separately. If the service deploys while a PR retains its merge base (or lags that base), this report still claims the merge base executed every round, so the central runtime-provenance result is unsupported and can be wrong. Persist and freeze an actual runtime/deployment revision instead.
findings.failureMode: A PR retains its merge base while the panel service is deployed or rolls back; `eval:continuity` still reports the merge-base SHA as the sole executing runtime.
findings.title: Do not relabel the PR merge base as the executing runtime

findings.description: The unknown-family check reads `fixture.families[appearance.family]`, so inherited `Object.prototype` names pass as known. The supported custom-fixture CLI accepts an appearance with `family: "toString"` and an empty `families` map, then reports one accepted family against zero real families and 100% blocking acceptance instead of rejecting the unsupported family. Use an own-property check and validate `families` before computing metrics.
findings.failureMode: Running `eval:continuity <fixture>` with an absent prototype-named family silently emits fabricated accepted-family and calibration counts.
findings.title: Require an own family entry during fixture validation

findings.description: `assertFixture` enters each run and validates only the two SHA fields; it never checks the `authority` discriminant that later drives both run totals. A custom fixture with the typo `authority: "authorative"` passes this boundary and emits `authoritativeRuns: 0` and `pendingReplayRuns: 0` for its one run instead of rejecting the unsupported record. Validate authority as exactly `authoritative` or `pending-replay` before computing metrics.
findings.failureMode: A typo or unsupported authority in a continuity fixture is silently omitted from both authority counts, producing a report whose run totals do not describe its input.
findings.title: Validate each run's authority before counting it

findings.description: Pinning the host to Factory 0.10 adopts a credential storage contract in which `data` is a string: even the plaintext encryptor returns `JSON.stringify(value)`, while configured encryption returns an envelope. `FactoryCredentialStore` still casts raw `data` directly to `AuthCredential`. Once Factory 0.10 creates or refreshes a credential, an enabled native reviewer loads a string and `factory-host` aborts boot with “has no OAuth login” (reproduced against the installed package). Decrypt/deserialize reads—and serialize encrypted refresh writes—with the same Factory encryption instance when adopting this pin.
findings.failureMode: A credential written by Factory 0.10 causes the panel's enabled-native-reviewer startup preflight to throw instead of loading OAuth credentials.
findings.title: Decode Factory 0.10 credential envelopes

findings.description: `runLane`'s `normalizeUsage` returns a non-null object after seeing even one counter and fills every missing counter with zero. Therefore a truncated/malformed provider response that exposes only input usage reaches this new predicate as `complete: true`, and the ensemble/baseline reports the synthesized lower bound as an exact total. Carry source-counter completeness from the lane (or validate all required counters here) rather than testing only for null.
findings.failureMode: A provider response containing `prompt_tokens` but omitting all completion/total usage produces an ensemble artifact whose usage.complete is true and whose total undercounts the call, corrupting cost/completeness reports.
findings.title: Do not equate any lane usage object with complete usage

findings.description: When candidates exist and both judge harnesses are actually attempted but fail, this catch emits `judgePromptHash: null` while preserving those calls in `judgeProvenance`. That is inconsistent with the success branch, which emits `hash(prompt)` even when `judgePath` had no candidates and made no judge call, and with the base implementation that always recorded the configured instruction hash. Emit the known shared hash for `JudgeAttemptFailure`; reserve null for a path where prompt selection itself failed.
findings.failureMode: A judge provider outage produces a failed ensemble artifact with null shared-prompt identity even though calls were made under the known adjudication instructions, breaking prompt-version audit/reporting for failed runs.
findings.title: Retain the judge instruction hash on attempted failures

findings.description: The pinned Mastra adapter retains provider counters under `result.usage.raw.raw` but recomputes top-level `totalTokens`. If xAI returns `prompt_tokens: 10`, `completion_tokens: 5`, and inconsistent `total_tokens: 20`, this line validates only the recomputed 15 and records the decision attempt as complete with total 15. Vendor responses reaching `packages/**` are explicitly untrusted; compare the retained raw counters and mark contradictory usage unknown instead of emitting a falsely complete record.
findings.failureMode: An inconsistent provider usage response bypasses the new total-consistency guards and produces a wrong, complete token total in harness and ensemble provenance.
findings.title: Validate retained raw usage before declaring it complete

findings.description: With `PANEL_JUDGE_HARNESS=native` (or a native fallback) and an explicitly blank `PANEL_JUDGE_NATIVE_MODEL`, lanes that return no findings now reach this base record and complete with `status: 'ok'` without ever calling `productionJudgeRoute`. Before this hunk, `productionModel()` was evaluated while constructing `base`, so the same run failed with the required-model configuration error. Validate the production route before the no-candidate fast path so a corpus cannot appear successful under an unusable judge configuration.
findings.failureMode: An invalid native judge configuration is silently accepted whenever successful reviewer lanes produce zero candidate findings, yielding a false successful ensemble/baseline record.
findings.title: Validate the judge route even when no candidate reaches it

findings.description: After `generateAdjudication` returns a completed attempt, JavaScript still executes the unchanged `finally`; if `FactoryCredentialStore.close()` rejects (for example during a transient database shutdown), that rejection replaces this return. `runEnsemble` then sees an ordinary error rather than `JudgeAttemptFailure`, emits empty `judgeProvenance` and zero judge usage, and loses the provider call this change is meant to account for. Preserve the completed attempt while handling/reporting cleanup failure separately, as the lane runner already does for its completed call record.
findings.failureMode: A credential-store close error after a completed judge call causes the ensemble failure record to omit the completed generation and its token usage.
findings.title: Do not discard a completed attempt when credential-store cleanup fails

findings.description: Factory's deployment parser decodes `FACTORY_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` as standard base64 and documents `openssl rand -base64 32`; a 32-byte output is padded with `=`. This canonical-base64url equality check rejects that shared key (and standard-base64 previous keys), so a correctly configured encrypted Factory cannot start Pilot/native credential access. Parse the same trimmed base64 format as Factory while still checking 32 decoded bytes.
findings.failureMode: An operator copies the Factory keyring generated/configured per Factory's own `openssl rand -base64 32` guidance into Pilot; `decodeKey` rejects the trailing `=` before constructing the store, and factory-host fails during module startup.
findings.title: Accept Factory's documented base64 key format

findings.description: This path enters `refreshLocked` without replacing or clearing an existing snapshot, and the handled `refreshToken` failure returns `undefined` without mutating it. If an org-preferred row replaces a cached user credential and the org token is expired/unrefreshable, `getApiKey` fails but `get(provider)` still exposes the old user token. The native OpenAI adapter awaits priming but then reads `get()` before deciding whether to refresh, so a still-unexpired stale token can be sent despite the live org row. Clear the snapshot on this failed live refresh, or make a failed prime stop consumers before they can read it.
findings.failureMode: A factory-automation store cached a user's fresh OpenAI credential, an expired org credential subsequently becomes selected, and its refresh fails; priming returns undefined but the request path reads and sends the cached user token, bypassing org-first credential selection and potentially using an account that was intentionally replaced.
findings.title: Clear stale snapshots when live OAuth refresh fails

findings.description: Registering `287` as a train fixture makes it loadable by the standard lane/scoring tooling, but this fixture tree has no `phase-a/dataset/diffs/287_*.diff`. For any run with an anchored finding near one of these labels, the standard `match.mjs --fixtures evals/golden/fixtures/mastra-287` path calls `scoreRun` without an inline diff, then `loadFrozenDiff` aborts with ENOENT before producing a score. Commit the aggregate diff at the standard dataset path so the retained scoring fixture is self-contained.
findings.failureMode: Rescoring a retained tag-287 lane run through the repository's standard match entry point exits with ENOENT instead of producing metrics.
findings.title: Include the scorer's frozen diff artifact

findings.description: This hunk stops asserting that `src/job-selection.js` is a validated control, but no scoring input or scorer path is changed to exclude findings for that file. On exact HEAD, a tag-287 run that hits all three labels plus the now-proven job-selection defect still reports four findings, `precision_strict: 0.75`, and score `0.77` (rather than three findings, precision 1, and score 1); a run containing only that defect also includes it in unmatched feedback. Thus future tag-287 benchmark runs still penalize correct reviewers despite this PR's quarantine. Add fixture-local exclusion metadata and consume it before candidate generation, metrics, and feedback, with a scorer-boundary regression test.
findings.failureMode: A benchmark run surfaces the real job-selection ordering defect; the scorer counts it as an unmatched false positive and lowers precision and score despite this PR classifying the case as an invalid negative control.
findings.title: Quarantine the invalid control in the scorer, not only this test

findings.description: This new proof shows that the frozen job-selection case is not a valid negative control, but the retained MASTRA-287 report still says the six-case fixture has a positive and paired negative control for each capability and publishes `Invalid control findings | 3 | 1` without noting that job-selection findings were misclassified. A developer consulting that report can therefore reuse this case or those aggregates as valid benchmark evidence, directly contradicting the new test. Add a MASTRA-297 correction beside the historical claims that identifies the quarantined case and marks the old invalid-finding/precision aggregates as uncorrected historical results.
findings.failureMode: A subsequent evaluation relies on the retained MASTRA-287 report and incorrectly treats the job-selection case and old aggregate statistics as validated negative-control evidence.
findings.title: Correct the report's negative-control claim

findings.description: The fixture declares `context.input.baseSha` as `runtimeProvenanceField` and publishes that value as every run's `executingRuntimeSha`, but `fetchPullRequestEvidence` assigns `baseSha` from GitHub's `merge_base_commit.sha`. If a PR was branched before the deployed factory revision (or deployment lags/advances independently), `eval:continuity` reports the merge base as the executing runtime and can falsely attribute the continuity result to the wrong deployed code. Capture and freeze an actual build/deployment revision in the run snapshot, then compute runtime provenance from that field.
findings.failureMode: For a panel run whose service build SHA differs from the PR merge base, the continuity report outputs the merge-base SHA as `executingRuntimeSha`, producing wrong provenance for the main evaluation result.
findings.title: Runtime provenance records the PR merge base, not the executing build

findings.description: The unknown-family guard uses a prototype-sensitive property lookup. A supplied fixture whose appearance names an undeclared family such as `toString` passes `assertFixture`; the evaluator then counts it as accepted even though `Object.keys(fixture.families)` and the real-family denominator do not include it (for an empty catalogue it emits `{accepted: 1, real: 0, rate: null}`). Require an own property with `Object.hasOwn(fixture.families, appearance.family)` after validating `families` as an object.
findings.failureMode: A continuity fixture containing an undeclared inherited Object key is accepted and produces impossible family counts instead of the promised `Unknown family` rejection.
findings.title: Inherited object keys bypass unknown-family validation

findings.description: This helper uses `Math.round` for half-tenth ties, while both existing golden metric implementations explicitly use round-half-to-even. Because `eval:continuity` accepts a fixture path, a valid slice with (for example) 1 accepted family out of 16 real families reports 6.3%, whereas the repository's published metric convention reports 6.2%; the same combined evaluation output therefore rounds equivalent ratios inconsistently. Reuse the established half-even percentage calculation.
findings.failureMode: A valid continuity fixture whose ratio lands exactly on an even half-tenth boundary emits a percentage 0.1 points higher than the repository's canonical metrics.
findings.title: Continuity percentages use different tie rounding from the metrics evaluator

findings.description: After `oauth.refreshToken` has successfully rotated the selected credential at the provider, this loop performs updates for every previous-key candidate in the same transaction. If an unrelated shadowed row's encryption/update fails, the catch rolls the whole transaction back, so the newly issued refresh token is discarded while the persisted old token may already be invalid. That permanently loses the selected OAuth grant and forces re-login even though its own write could have succeeded. Persist the refreshed selected row without making it contingent on opportunistic shadow rewrites (then rotate the other rows separately).
findings.failureMode: An expired OAuth refresh succeeds, but rewriting any shadowed previous-key row fails; rollback leaves only the now-invalid old refresh token in storage.
findings.title: Do not couple shadow rewrites to a rotating OAuth refresh

findings.description: Unlike the base implementation, the new path does not put the just-read credential into the snapshot before attempting refresh, and this failure branch returns without clearing the prior snapshot. If Factory replaces cached credential A with expired credential B, B's refresh fails, and the database is then unavailable, the degraded-read catch serves still-unexpired A even though a successful authoritative read already showed it was superseded. Clear/update the snapshot on the live read or explicitly invalidate it on refresh failure so an outage cannot resurrect the old credential.
findings.failureMode: A credential is replaced, its first refresh fails, then the database is unavailable; a later call serves the superseded cached token instead of failing closed.
findings.title: Invalidate stale snapshots when refresh fails

findings.description: The newly added shadow-row UPDATE ignores the command result, so a PostgreSQL RLS policy or BEFORE UPDATE trigger that silently suppresses that row is treated as a successful key rotation. The old-key envelope remains; once the previous key is retired, `resolve` decrypts every candidate and rejects credential access even though the selected row is current and valid. Request `rowCount` from the query seam and require exactly one affected row before considering each rewrite successful.
findings.failureMode: A lower-priority previous-key row is visible to SELECT but an UPDATE policy/trigger suppresses its rewrite; after key retirement the unrotated shadow row blocks all access.
findings.title: Verify each credential rewrite affected its row

findings.description: The locked re-read now selects and locks both audience candidates, whereas the base path locked only the selected row. If the lower-priority row is held by an unrelated Factory transaction for longer than `lock_timeout`, refreshing an expired higher-priority OAuth row also times out; recovery merely polls unlocked reads, so that selected row remains expired and access eventually fails even though it was independently available. Lock/refresh the selected scope first and rotate shadow rows separately.
findings.failureMode: A lower-priority credential row is contended while the selected OAuth credential is expired; the selected credential cannot be refreshed and the model call times out.
findings.title: Do not let a shadow-row lock block the selected refresh

findings.description: When the initial credential is an API key that needs key rotation, `getApiKey` calls `refreshLocked(provider)` without an OAuth provider. A concurrent Factory update can replace it with a valid OAuth credential before the locked re-read (or before lock-timeout recovery); the method then snapshots the OAuth credential but the optional `oauth?.getApiKey` at lines 145/161 returns `undefined`, so the current model request fails despite a usable token. Resolve `getOAuthProvider(provider)` from the post-lock credential or pass it into this path.
findings.failureMode: A credential changes from a previous-key API key to unexpired OAuth between the unlocked and locked SELECT, and getApiKey returns undefined for one request.
findings.title: Resolve OAuth after the locked re-read

findings.description: This credentials feature changes the runtime Mastra/Factory cohort (`@mastra/code-sdk`, core, Factory, pg, and CLI) even though the repository hard rule requires upstream version bumps to be isolated dependency PRs. The bootstrap exception does not apply because the base already had contract tests pinning both the provider cohort and Factory. Merging this as one unit removes the required independent adoption/rollback boundary: a credential fix cannot be reverted without also rolling the host across the upstream cohort (and vice versa). Move the manifest, lockfile, and patch pin updates to their own dependency PR.
findings.failureMode: An incident requiring rollback of either the credential feature or the upstream cohort cannot be isolated because both changes are merged as one feature commit boundary.
findings.title: Split the upstream cohort bump from this feature

findings.description: Live CLI accepts `--report` equal to `--ledger` (or an alias to it). After a successful five-call run, this `writeFile` truncates the just-created JSONL ledger and replaces it with the summary report; using the plan path similarly destroys the registered plan. Validate canonicalized plan, ledger, and report paths are pairwise distinct before opening or invoking providers.
findings.failureMode: A valid live invocation such as `--plan plan.json --ledger evidence.jsonl --report evidence.jsonl` completes paid calls and then irreversibly overwrites its audit ledger.
findings.title: Reject colliding output paths before execution

findings.description: A `micro-pilot-result` row is enough to enter replay mode, but the code runs Ax before proving that every required adjudication/proposal cache row is present and consistent. If one cached row is missing from an otherwise completed ledger, `AdjudicationAdapter` falls through to `Calls.invoke`, opens the credential store, and makes a new paid provider request; only afterward can the `calls.cursor !== 0` replay check run. Preflight the complete replay inventory and preserved result before constructing/running Ax.
findings.failureMode: Replaying a completed ledger with one deleted cached operation unexpectedly appends rows and spends a provider call instead of refusing without credentials or writes.
findings.title: Validate completed replay inventory before compiling

findings.description: The preflight at line 83 throws `failed-ledger` for an existing failure or incomplete intent, but this catch then appends another `micro-pilot-failure` because `prior` is absent and rows already exist. A retry that should only refuse therefore changes the preserved evidence bytes on every attempt. Track whether this invocation appended the header/intent, or exclude preflight refusals from the catch append.
findings.failureMode: Invoking the CLI again with a failed or incomplete ledger appends a new failure row instead of leaving the audit artifact byte-for-byte unchanged.
findings.title: Do not mutate an already failed ledger

findings.description: The live path records only `git rev-parse HEAD` and never checks `git status`; dry-run likewise builds directly from working-tree fixtures. With an uncommitted edit to a source case or prompt, deterministic reconstruction still passes against those dirty bytes while the manifest and ledger attribute them to the unchanged commit SHA, producing false run provenance. Perform the existing clean-clone preflight before building or executing either mode.
findings.failureMode: Running the CLI from a dirty checkout creates a plan/ledger whose revision claims a commit that does not contain the evaluated inputs or instruction.
findings.title: Refuse dirty source before attributing the run

findings.description: Completed replay compares only `result`; it returns `prior.report` without deriving it again from the preserved terminal rows. If the result row's report is corrupted while the operation evidence remains intact, replay succeeds and emits false call/token/wall-time totals. Recompute `report(ledger.rows)` and require it to match the stored report before returning.
findings.failureMode: Editing only `micro-pilot-result.report.totalTokens` in a completed ledger makes a zero-call replay print that incorrect total instead of detecting ledger damage.
findings.title: Recompute and verify the replayed cost report

findings.description: The live call has no timeout or `AbortSignal`. If the native provider request stalls without resolving or rejecting, execution hangs indefinitely with only an incomplete intent in the ledger, so no terminal/failure report is produced and the lock remains held until external termination. Wrap each operation in a bounded abort controller and pass its signal to `generateText`, as the existing pilot does.
findings.failureMode: A reachable network/provider stall leaves the micro-pilot permanently running and its ledger locked rather than ending with typed failure evidence.
findings.title: Bound live provider calls with an abort signal

findings.description: For the default native OpenAI judge, `@ai-sdk/openai` populates `response.modelId` from the provider's `response.created.response.model`, and Mastra also tags that response as provider `openai.responses`. When the reported ID equals the requested bare model (the normal successful case), this condition discards it, so `judgeModelReported` is emitted as null despite direct provider evidence. Preserve `response.modelId` when response metadata proves it came from this provider (rather than accepting only IDs that differ from configuration).
findings.failureMode: A normal OpenAI native adjudication returns response.created.model = gpt-5.6-sol for requested openai/gpt-5.6-sol; decisionGenerationMetadata returns modelReported null and the ensemble emits the wrong identity metadata.
findings.title: Preserve matching provider-reported model IDs

findings.description: This branch now runs before any call to `productionJudgeRoute()`, while the deleted `productionModel()` call used to validate the route unconditionally. With `PANEL_JUDGE_NATIVE_MODEL=''` and successful lanes that all report no findings, `runEnsemble` emits an `ok` record without rejecting the unusable native-judge configuration. Resolve/validate the production route before this early return, while still sourcing recorded model identity from provenance.
findings.failureMode: An ensemble run configured with a blank required native judge model and zero reviewer findings succeeds instead of failing configuration validation.
findings.title: Validate the judge route before the no-findings return

findings.description: Raising the supported Factory floor to 0.10 leaves `FactoryCredentialStore` casting `model_provider_credentials.data` directly to `AuthCredential`, but Factory 0.10's plaintext encryptor returns `JSON.stringify(value)` and the PG factory backend JSON-serializes that again, so new/updated JSONB rows are read back as strings (real encryption also stores an envelope string). With any enabled native reviewer, `load()` returns that string and `assertNativeCredentials` throws during startup; `getApiKey()` is likewise unusable. Decrypt with the same Factory secret-encryption instance before consuming rows, and encrypt refreshed writes.
findings.failureMode: With any enabled native reviewer and a credential newly saved by Factory 0.10, factory-host boot throws during credential preflight because the DB JSONB value is a string rather than an AuthCredential object.
findings.title: Decrypt Factory 0.10 credential rows before using them

findings.description: `severityDispositionErrors` compares only the blocking flag with the final disposition and never compares `finding.reportedSeverity` with `family.consequenceSeverity`. Thus a panel finding reported as critical whose adjudicated consequence is high validates successfully but leaves this metric unchanged (2 rather than 3). Include severity disagreement in this predicate so the advertised severity-error metric is accurate.
findings.failureMode: A calibrated finding has the wrong reported severity but the correct blocking disposition, and the main calibration report incorrectly records no severity error.
findings.title: Count severity mismatches in the error metric

findings.description: The Open SWE branch checks the comment's kind/content but ignores the stored `source.reviewId`. Consequently a finding comment from review 5035882999 can be attached to a session whose authoritative review is 5036180576; validation succeeds and the first-pass finding is then reported in a later-round phase-matched comparison. Require each Open SWE finding source's `reviewId` to equal `session.reviewId`.
findings.failureMode: A review comment is assigned to the wrong Open SWE session/head, passes validation, and corrupts phase and repetition metrics.
findings.title: Bind Open SWE findings to their session review

findings.description: `dispositionSourceArtifactId` is checked only for existence, not that the referenced artifact is classified as `disposition-evidence`. A corpus can change a proven family's disposition, point this field at an ordinary development review, pass validation, and publish corrupted precision; against the shipped corpus this changes the combined rate from 60% to 40%. Require the source artifact's disposition-evidence status (whether issue comment or review comment).
findings.failureMode: A malformed or edited calibration corpus cites an ordinary review as its disposition source, passes validation, and produces incorrect adjudication metrics.
findings.title: Require disposition-evidence status

findings.description: The raw-source projection handles only reviews and review comments, so `operator-disposition` artifacts—the evidence used for final family labels—are never compared with the frozen `:issue-comments` response. Replacing an operator artifact's body with fabricated text and recomputing its self-hash still passes validation. Project issue comments too and require every disposition artifact to match its authoritative raw item.
findings.failureMode: Tampered or incorrectly extracted operator disposition evidence is accepted as source-backed calibration data.
findings.title: Bind operator dispositions to raw issue comments

findings.description: The record-level base/head/merge SHAs are only syntax-checked and are never compared with the `:pull` raw source. Replacing `source.baseSha` with any other 40-hex value passes validation, so a corpus can advertise false PR provenance despite retaining authoritative pull bytes. Parse the expected pull source and compare its PR number and SHAs to `record.source`.
findings.failureMode: An incorrectly extracted or edited PR source SHA is accepted, making the calibration corpus report false commit provenance.
findings.title: Bind record SHAs to the frozen pull response

findings.description: A panel session requires one review and one panel record, but never checks that they represent the same review. On PR 194, replacing the panel review artifact/ID with the same-head Open SWE review 5024251212 still validates while the findings actually come from panel record 5024223847. For non-snapshot sessions, require the panel-record identity to match `session.reviewId`.
findings.failureMode: A panel record is attributed to a different same-head GitHub review, and the corpus accepts false session provenance.
findings.title: Bind panel records to the panel review ID
